#2697. Lakers forward has ‘a lot of special things’ planned being back in LA

Ziaire Williams takes pride in giving back to the local community. NBAE via Getty Images

#2695. Arman Tsarukyan OK With Volkanovski vs. Gaethe on 1 Condition

UFC lightweight contender Arman Tsarukyan is OK with Alexander Volkanovski fighting Justin Gaethje next, on one condition.

Tsarukyan is the No. 1 contender in the UFC lightweight division to Gaethje's lightweight belt, but the organization is said to be seriously considering booking Gaethje against Volkanovski next in a superfight between champions.

Tsarukyan says that's just fine with him, but on one condition: that Gaethje vacates his belt.

Speaking to MMAFighting.com, Tsarukyan said that he's fine with Gaethje fighting Volkanovski next, but only if Gaethje gives up his belt, because Tsarukyan is tired of waiting for his long-awaited title shot.

"If Gaethje wants to fight Volkanovski, he's got to leave the belt and do like a random fight without the title because I'm the number one contender and the UFC told me that I'm fighting for the belt. I don't think they're going to do something else," Tsarukyan said (via Bloody Elbow).

With Gaethje and Volkanovski both 38 years old and nearing the end of their respective MMA careers, a superfight between these two for all the marbles does make a lot of sense, as both can walk away into the sunset afterwards.

But, as Tsarukyan said, if that's what the UFC wants to do, then he still wants to fight for the title, though it would be against someone else — potentially someone like Paddy Pimblett or Ilia Topuria.

So we will have to wait and see what the UFC wants to do with the lightweight division, and first, we need to find out what Gaethje himself wants to do, as he's been on the fence about whether or not he wants to fight again or retire from mixed martial arts.

Gaethje is coming off the best win of his career over Topuria at UFC Freedom 250, so if he retires now, he'd be walking away on top of his game. But at the same time, he'd also be leaving a lot of money on the table, which is why a Volkanovski superfight makes so much sense.

#2691. Messi's defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs

Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi's Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday.

Rodriguez's goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida.

Defending the MLS Cup was the last chance the ambitious franchise co-owned by David Beckham had to salvage its season after falling in the round of 16 of the CONCACAF Champions Cup and in the group stage of the Leagues Cup.

The only trophy that made it into Miami's cabinet this year was the Campeones Cup, the annual matchup between the champions of MLS and the Mexican league.

For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS's top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested.

In 2024 Miami stumbled against Atlanta United before earning their first MLS Cup crown last year.

The star-studded side featuring Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul as well as Messi, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio.

German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar.

"For me, the defeat is totally unfair because I think the team rose to the occasion, we deserved to win it throughout the whole match," said Miami coach Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez. "The clearest chances were ours, but that's football.

"The opponents defended well, too. Even though Leo didn't have a shot on target, we created a lot of chances."

The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter's defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

Miami's early exit extends the champion's curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012.

Gonzalez shook up his starting lineup, leaving Suarez on the bench in favor of young Brazilian Riquelme Fillipi in a change that gave Miami's attack a spark in the first half.

But Messi made an uncharacteristic error in the box after a pinpoint pass from Berterame and Columbus keeper Patrick Schulte came up with a series of saves.

Columbus came close to scoring in the 65th when St. Clair saved a header from Gonzalo Tapia and Miami's Micael blocked the quick follow-up from Brais Mendez.

Gonzalez inserted Suarez with 15 minutes remaining, but Miami still couldn't capitalize on their chances. A Casemiro header was disallowed for offside and Berterame missed a header.

In the day's only other contest, Emmanuel Sabbi's 58th-minute goal lifted the Vancouver Whitecaps to a 1-0 victory over Real Salt Lake for a 2-0 sweep of their first-round series.

#2690. 5 questions with a Chargers expert: What to expect from D.J. Uiagalelei?

On paper, the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers are quite familiar with one another: they last met in January, in the wild card round of the NFL playoffs. However, there have been quite a few changes since that game, especially at the most important position on the field.

Tommy DeVito will start at quarterback for New England in place of Drake Maye, while Justin Herbert's absence as Chargers QB will allow D.J. Uiagalelei to get his first career start. To learn more about him, and the rest of the Chargers in 2026, we spoke with Michael Peterson of Pats Pulpit's sister site Bolts From the Blue, the SB Nation community for all things Chargers.

1. With Justin Herbert missing this game due to a concussion, what can you tell us about backup D.J. Uiagalelei's strengths and weaknesses?

So D.J. Uiagalelei has made massive strides since coming out of college. The fact he has been able to stay with a NFL team this long is truly a testament to that because he was — to put it bluntly — a horrendous passer to end his collegiate career. With a full year and more behind Herbert, mainly as the third-stringer, he's progressed enough to be a serviceable player for an emergency situation like this.

As a passer, he is fairly composed in the pocket and has enough athleticism to escape and extend plays. He also plays with some notable confidence and will not think twice about attempting a tough throw. However, he's not reckless with the football. He knows when to pull it down and get yards on the ground when possible. In his first NFL action in garbage time against the Texans, he helped bring the offense down the field and even threw his first professional touchdown on a great rip over the middle.

His biggest weakness will be that he's still a wildcard and an unknown in this league. He could be serviceable like I mentioned, but he could also flail in the moment like most young passers in their first career starts.

I think Mike Vrabel would be wise to turn up the heat early and often and hope the second-year UDFA crumbles under the pressure.

2. Why has it taken so long for Omarion Hampton to start breaking out, and what challenges does he present for a defense?

Hampton unfortunately did not help himself this year by beginning the campaign with back-to-back games where he lost a fumble. It also did not help that he lost those fumbles in pivotal moments that directly led to the Chargers losing said games. It unfortunately took a bit for him to get back into the god graces of Mike McDaniel and now he seems to be off and running with a renewed energy. He's been phenomenal and looks every bit the player the Chargers wanted to take in the first round.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

As a runner, Hampton's skillset is not designed to make someone miss by being shifty. He's going to make them miss by running full speed through the weak point of your tackle attempt to consistently gain extra yards and fall forward at the end of runs. He's the type of runner that will get the most out of the minor creases given to him and when the defense is worn down by the fourth quarter, he'll look to keep pounding it even more. Patriots should come prepared to try and get him stopped before his momentum builds, not unlike how the Chargers kept Derrick Henry in check during their lone win of the season.

3. LT Joe Alt is a Pro Bowler, but the rest of the Chargers' offensive line consists of rookies and backups. Where are the non-Alt bright spots up front, and who do you expect the Patriots to try to exploit?

One guy who went from roster afterthought to solid starter the past few weeks has been rookie left guard Logan Taylor. He was a sixth-round pick out of Boston College this year and mainly was used at tackle during the preseason despite guard be the obvious place for him in the NFL. Once he settled in after being forced into the starting lineup, he's been one of the lone bright spots outside of Alt. Another recent bright spot has also been the return of Kayode Awosika who, after being the original starter at left guard before his fibula injury, is now starting at right guard over Cole Strange (who should have been benched a long time ago).

Both of the guard spots being reinforced has led to back-to-back strong rushing games for Hampton, as well as two consecutive intereption-less games by Herbert.

As far as which player up front the Patriots should exploit, it has to be rookie right tackle Travis Burke. As good as Burke has been in the run game, he is quite a bit behind as far as pass protection fundamentals. He is athletic enough to stay outside, but he lacks proper set points and punch mechanics. He gets beat by twitchier rushers and overall speed that can threaten his corner more than he likes. He is coming off a horrible game against David Bailey and the Jets and the Patriots should do their best to exploit that side of the line this week.

4. What has contributed to the Chargers' struggles stopping opposing passing games? Are there any defenders the Patriots should try to avoid?

Against the Jets, the absence of cornerback Tarheeb Still was felt, especially when injuries have continued to rear their head in a position group that is terribly shallow. Undrafted rookie Rodney Shelley has played a lot this season and his production has been abysmal. Even veteran Donte Jackson, who has battled multiple injuries this year, is still very feast-or-famine.

The absence of Derwin James has also been apparent. He's a back-to-back second-team All-Pro slot defender and anyone who knows ball understands how good an elite slot player can be for a defense. The Chargers have been getting by — for the most part — with a group of guys no one has probably heard of at the second and third levels. The Jets game was a bit of a fluke, but they'll have to right the ship fast to avoid making that result less of "who they are" and more of that fluke I just mentioned.

5. It seems there is some disconnect between Jim Harbaugh, Mike McDaniel, and Justin Herbert. What is happening with the Chargers' current leadership structure, and who do you see remaining in L.A. when the dust settles?

What some may not understand about Harbaugh's role as the head coach is that he is a true CEO. He does not have a hand in helping scheme either side of the ball. He makes his hires and then he allows how coaches to coach. That's a major reason why no coordinator has been fired or changed during the season under his leadership and it's the main reason why McDaniel was never going to be fired. There's no one to pick up the slack and Harbaugh sure wasn't going to step in and start calling plays for the first time in decades.

When it's all said and done, Harbaugh will most likely remain, even if he truly should not. The team will owe him a ton of money over the next two years and the Spanos family will not want to fork out money to a coach that's no longer working for him. Harbaugh's two 11-win seasons prior to this year still gives him some grace, but with how bad this year is, there will be no more grace for him should this disaster continue into the 2027 season.

#2683. Lakers player grades: L.A. falls short to Spurs in NBA Cup showdown

The Los Angeles Lakers headed to Frost Bank Center to face the San Antonio Spurs in an NBA Cup group-play showdown on Friday at full strength. Austin Reaves, who had missed each of their last five games with a bruised heel, was cleared to play, and they likely felt they had a great chance of coming away with a victory.

Early on, it certainly looked like they were on their way to toppling the defending Western Conference champions. An 11-2 run in the last four minutes and change of the first quarter gave them a 27-14 lead at the end of the period, and they still led 54-38 at halftime. The Lakers held the Spurs to 42.5% shooting in the first half, and the Spurs only made two shots outside the paint during that time.

But L.A.'s offense became icy in the third quarter. The Spurs scored 13 unanswered points late in the third quarter and in the opening moments of the fourth period to go up 82-78, and then they took an 81-73 lead with 7:19 left in the fourth quarter. L.A. kept fighting, but with under a minute left, it gave up an offensive rebound off a missed free throw by Victor Wembanyama and left Stephon Castle open, allowing Castle to hit a 3-pointer for a 96-90 San Antonio advantage.

The Lakers then got a trey from Reaves and forced a double-dribble violation by De'Aaron Fox. Forward Jake LaRavia was intentionally fouled to prevent a 3-point attempt, and he made both ensuing free throws. Fox then made two foul shots after being intentionally fouled, and Quentin Grimes, after being intentionally fouled himself with 3.9 seconds to go, made his first free throw and missed the second one, resulting in a 99-96 Lakers loss.

For the game, the Lakers shot just 43% from the field and 28.6% from 3-point range, and they made just 35.6% of their overall attempts after halftime. They also gave up 13 offensive rebounds and 20 second-chance points while being outscored 17-5 in fast-break points.

They now hold a 15-4 record, while San Antonio is now tied with the Philadelphia 76ers for the NBA's best record at 16-4. As a result of Friday's loss, Los Angeles will not advance to the knockout rounds of the Emirates NBA Cup.

Thybulle helped muck things up defensively with four steals and one block in 21 minutes, but he contributed nothing offensively. He missed all four of his shot attempts, and all four of them came from beyond the arc. He went scoreless and had two rebounds and two assists.

LaRavia had a decent offensive effort by making three of his seven field-goal attempts, two of his four 3-point tries and two of his three free throw attempts to score 10 points in 34 minutes. But the Lakers needed more help from him on the boards. He got only three rebounds after coming into this game averaging 4.4 rebounds in 25.9 minutes a game.

Kessler scored 10 points on 3-of-5 shooting from the field, and he grabbed 13 rebounds, with eight of them coming on the offensive boards. He did a fairly good job of boxing out and giving Los Angeles additional shot opportunities.

He also had four assists, one block and one steal. Defensively, Kessler did a decent job on Wembanyama, who had 25 points and 16 rebounds but shot just 10-of-25 from the field.

Reaves was rusty early in this game, and he even airballed a 3-point attempt. He missed four shot attempts and had four turnovers before he made his first basket with 3:10 to go in the second quarter.

But from that point on, he mostly looked like his usual self. He ended up with 21 points on 8-of-15 overall shooting while hitting five of his nine attempts from 3-point range, and 13 of those points came in the fourth quarter to keep the Lakers' hopes alive.

Reaves, however, committed seven turnovers and had just one assist, although he was great on the boards with eight rebounds in 36 minutes.

Doncic scored 14 points in the first quarter, although he missed all six of his 3-point attempts during that time. Unfortunately, he cooled off considerably after halftime, going 3-of-9 from the field in the third quarter. He ended up 14-of-31 from the field for 31 points.

His 3-point shooting has become very concerning lately. Against San Antonio, he missed all but one of his 13 attempts from that distance, and he has now gone 13-of-64 from that distance in his last five games. He had shot 40.6% from downtown in his first 12 games of this season.

Doncic did help out in other areas on Friday, as he finished with six rebounds, eight assists and three steals.

Sexton helped spark the Lakers with nine first-half points on 4-of-5 shooting. But they could've used more firepower from him after halftime. He finished with 12 points on 5-of-10 shooting, plus four rebounds and one block, in 15 minutes.

In 26 minutes, Grimes was fairly efficient with nine points on 3-of-6 shooting and 2-of-4 from 3-point land, to go along with one assist, one steal and one block in 26 minutes. But this was a game during which L.A. needed plenty more offense from him, especially down the stretch and especially with Doncic struggling to find the basket often enough.

Williams was another player who needed to produce more than he did. He missed all three of his shot attempts and went scoreless, and he finished with two rebounds and three assists in 16 minutes.

In this game, Mamukelashvili finally made his first 3-pointer since Nov. 11 versus Milwaukee Bucks. But that was the only basket he made in five attempts. He finished with three points, four rebounds, one steal and one block in 13 minutes.

In six minutes, Vanderbilt went scoreless and had one rebound, and he had a nice contest of a Dylan Harper layup attempt in the third quarter, forcing Harper to come up well short of the rim.

#2680. 3 Observations from Indiana men’s basketball’s 93-57 win over Bowling Green

Indiana men's basketball dominated Bowling Green tonight, going on a run just over five minutes into the game that effectively put the Falcons to bed. The Hoosiers were shooting well, defending well, and rebounding well in what may have been the most complete performance from this group so far.

Though it wasn't a marquee win like last week's victories over Arkansas or Kentucky, the margin of victory was one that boosted Indiana's computer profile. KenPom only favored Indiana by 20 entering the game, so the blowout moved Indiana up five spots in the national ranking.

At 8-0, Indiana looks much improved over Darian DeVries' first season, with KenPom now projecting the Hoosiers to win 23 games and go 12-8 in Big Ten play.

Indiana had a season-high 18 assists tonight against Bowling Green, starting to resemble the fast-paced offense we saw from DeVries' group last year. While Indiana has more players that are capable of creating unassisted buckets, the ball movement tonight helped the Hoosiers take more quality looks from the perimeter, something that will be important for maintaining a respectable 3-point percentage this season.

Bryce Lindsay's deep shot against Arkansas will go down as a high-point of the season, but over the last couple games Indiana had gotten into the habit of chucking a few too many heat checks from deep or taking transition threes that negate the team's rebounding advantage.

Seeing the way the ball moved tonight was an encouraging step for this group not just cause it made the offense look a little better, but because it reflects well on the team's chemistry so early in the season. With a team full of transfers, having nine different players record an assist in a game is no small feat.

Aiden Sherrell had one of his stronger performances of the season, finishing with 16 points, nine rebounds, two blocks and an assist. He also went 2-6 from 3-point range.

Tonight's performance was a good example of why he's a potential NBA player. A seven footer who can score from the perimeter, rebound on both ends of the floor, and protect the rim is a valuable piece for any team. After an impressive year last year at Bama, he's averaging more points and shooting better from deep this year at Indiana.

Even though he cooled off by the end of the night, his early threes are exactly what Indiana will need from him going forward. Establishing himself as a threat at the beginning of the game will force defenses to account for him until the final whistle.

It's hard to say enough good things about Bryce Lindsay so far this year. Against Bowling Green, he scored 18 points, grabbed five rebounds, had three assists, and also added two steals. He was also super efficient, going 2/4 from 3-point range and making all of his free throws.

What I like most about Lindsay's game is his ability to be what DeVries needs on the floor, no matter who he's playing with. He can play point guard alongside Darren Harris at the shooting guard spot, or play shooting guard next to Markus Burton.

Calling him the sixth man doesn't even feel right, as he plays the fifth most minutes on the team, but he's been a huge asset for DeVries and Indiana this year, doing everything asked of him, and then some.

#2678. Steelers locker room 'prideful' but muted after win amid Aaron Rodgers firestorm

PITTSBURGH – Pat Freiermuth found himself in the center of the mess involving the Steelers and now-former quarterback Aaron Rodgers this week.

Rodgers told ESPN's "Pat McAfee Show" that the veteran tight end was the player who informed him coach Mike McCarthy was benching him in favor of Mason Rudolph late Tuesday night, Nov. 24.

Rodgers went on to say a lot of other explosive things about McCarthy, general manager Omar Khan and owner Art Rooney II over the course of his rambling 34-minute interview that captivated the NFL world.

Required reading: T.J. Watt, Steelers defense make statement in first game without Aaron Rodgers

You know the themes by now. Rodgers said McCarthy was sleeping in meetings and slacking on his film study. He called McCarthy unhealthy and unfit to be calling the offense for a team in the heat of a race for a playoff spot in the AFC. Et cetera, et cetera.

It was noteworthy, then, when Freiermuth was one of the players to address the situation most directly in the locker room after his team cruised to a 27-5 victory against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday afternoon at Acrisure Stadium.

"Pretty tough. I'm not going to lie. It was pretty tough," he said when asked how he's felt the past couple of days. "A lot of emotions. Just really, just sad. It was just a sad situation. We've just got to move on. Aaron's still one of my closest friends, but we just have to continue to move on and keep winning."

Most of his teammates tried to stay away from it, obliquely referencing the difficulty of the preparation amid a national firestorm while trying to keep the focus on what happened on the field.

That emotion was palpable, though. The room cleared out pretty quickly. Post-game victory music lasted maybe 10 minutes between the end of the game and media arriving for post-game interviews. Right tackle Brock Hoffman wasn't even sure who'd received the game ball, if one was awarded. There were few hoots and fewer hollers.

Not quite the scene you'd expect after what should have been a rousing home victory against one of the top teams in the conference. One the Steelers could see again in the postseason as they seek their first playoff win since 2016.

"Prideful" was the word Freiermuth used to describe how he was feeling about the result.

Earlier in the week, he'd delivered a fiery speech to the offense. He's one of the unit's most tenured players, with most of six seasons in Pittsburgh under his belt. He was glad to see his group respond with some explosive plays that complemented two defensive touchdowns in a game that was never really close.

"I was feeling passionate about what was going on," he said. "It was more from the heart of what the Steelers mean to me, and to my family and the Rooney family. And, just in general, nobody cares what we're going through at all, so we're either going to act soft about it or go out there and do something about it."

Hoffman found the comments "motivating" and felt they added energy to what was left of the short week of practice after the bombshell of the Rodgers news had landed, then settled.

The team rallied around quarterback Mason Rudolph, who completed nine of his 15 passes for 142 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions in Rodgers' place. The running game added 117 yards to control the clock.

"Obviously, the whole world was laughing at us," Hoffman said. "I'm not going to comment on that situation, but it felt like everybody was kind of counting us out. And for us to come in here, still stay undefeated at home and beat a really good Broncos team? You can't write that any better."

A turning point this week was what coach Mike McCarthy called a "players council" meeting after Rodgers was benched, where many parties apparently spoke freely about what was and wasn't working for the team that had been mired in a two-game losing streak against Cincinnati and Philadelphia.

McCarthy had touted it as productive in responding to Rodgers' comments, but few players really had their chance to tell their side of the story.

Freiermuth said he appreciated it while implying, as Rodgers explicitly said in his interview, that some of it was overdue.

"We were able to have grown conversations," he said. "We were able to hold each other accountable and talk to each other about what we want to fix. Or what we can do better as a team, as players, as coaches. Really impressive about the conversations we've had this week. The asks, the wants that coaches and players see. And it was just great to put it together in a win and have those tough conversations. Because at the end of the day, when stuff happens and you talk it through, you're able to get closer."

It's therefore possible that these Steelers are fixable. They now sit at 7-4, a half-game behind the Bengals in the AFC North standings.

Their schedule down the stretch is manageable. Jacksonville is the only remaining opponent with a winning record, so there's a runway for this team to position itself well if it can continue to come together.

Freiermuth pointedly stopped short of praising McCarthy, however, when asked how it felt to deliver a win for him personally. That felt noteworthy, given his proximity to Rodgers, and indicated that there's probably quite a bit of healing still to come in a locker room that seems to lack buoyancy, even if the most recent result feels satisfying.

"Obviously that's tough for him and his family," Freiermuth said of the criticism McCarthy has faced in the wake of Rodgers' comments. "We just wanted to win in general."

#2676. Kentucky coach Mark Pope takes responsibility after Wildcats attempt illegal play in upset loss to Wichita State

An overtime game was already shaping up to be a bad night for Kentucky head coach Mark Pope. Then it got so much worse.

Facing unranked Wichita State on Friday, the Wildcats found themselves down by two with 5.4 seconds remaining in overtime. They had the ball and a chance to win, however, with Alex Wilkins inbounding the ball from their baseline after a Wichita State timeout.

Then something bizarre happened. Once Wilkins was given the ball, he passed the ball to Kentucky guard Mason Williams, who had run out of bounds on the baseline. The intention was clearly some trickery to find a soft spot in the Shockers' defense.

The result, however, was a turnover. The play was clearly illegal, with both members of the ESPN booth immediately saying, "They can't do that."

Both the Kentucky players and crowd were clearly confused for understandable reasons once the officials called the play dead. Another person stunned by the turn of events was Wichita State head coach Paul Mills, as he told reporters after the game:

"To be honest with you, we thought it was going to be Alex Wilkins going up the right side of the floor. So, when they ran the inbounds play off of a dead ball, I was like, 'That's not legal.'"

So, what happened? Pope took full responsibility for the play after the game, telling reporters that a brain fart caused him to forget the circumstances of the play:

"That's 100% on me, guys. That is 100% me. Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind and I messed that up. It was really costly. It's a tough one to carry as a coach for sure.

When Pope says he thought the play was a live ball, he's referring to an inbounds play immediately after a made basket, which is the one kind of inbounds play in which players are allowed to run along the baseline and even pass to another player who can then inbound the ball.

In every other circumstance, including out of a timeout, the ball is fixed. The inbounder can't move, and he certainly can't give the ball to another player out of bounds.

Making the situation even more wild is that Kentucky very nearly won the game after that. Wichita State inbounded the ball, but an errant pass resulted in a steal for Ousmane N'Diaye, who then passed the ball to Milan Momcilovic for a would-be game-winner. The shot clanked away, though, giving Wichita State the win.

It was a mortifying way to lose a basketball game, before you even consider that Kentucky also blew a 14-point lead in the first half and committed even more mistakes down the stretch.

Add all that to the fact that Kentucky is now 4-3 after tying for seventh place in the SEC last season and that one of those wins was a one-point survival against Northern Arizona. For a program like Kentucky, that's more than enough to put you on the hot seat.

#2675. Undrafted rookie could be the Rams best option at tight end

After making a move towards multiple tight ends late last season, it was not surprising that the Los Angeles Rams brought eight tight ends into OTAs and kept them all through training camp. L.A. finally decided to keep five, a higher than average number, on the opening roster. They also kept around another tight end, prospect Dan Villari, on the practice squad.

Spring forward to the end of November and the Rams deep tight end room has been thinned substantially by injuries. Terrance Ferguson is out for the year; Colby Parkinson has missed one full game, parts of another half-dozen, and obviously impaired in many others; Davis Allen has a high ankle sprain, which carries a normal recovery time of a minimum of four weeks; and now Tyler Higbee has been designated as week-to-week with a bruised chest. Against the Green Packers on Thanksgiving Eve, the Rams installed offensive tackle David Quessenberry as tight end in the "13" personnel groupings.

Villari, 24 years-old, was signed by the Rams as a 2026 undrafted free agent out of Syracuse, but his journey to the NFL did not begin as a tight end. Originally recruited and signed as a quarterback by Michigan, he spent two seasons with the Wolverines. After a redshirt, he appeared in four 2021 games, recording one completion in three attempt and running for 35 yards on nine carries.

Transferred to Syracuse for 2022 and the Orangemen converted him to tight end in summer workouts. Over four seasons, he played in 44 games with 25 starts, catching 64 passes for 671 yards. In 2023 and 24, Syracuse, lined him up all over the field, collecting reps at running back and quarterback to go along with tight end duties. For his career, he chipped in 484 rushing yards at a 4.9 per carry clip and completed 23 of 33 passes for 177 yards.

It's fair to label him as a receiver first prospect. At 6'4" 243 lb.Villari is not a towering tight end like the rest of the unit. He sports just-above average arm length at 32 1/4" and owns good-sized hands, 9 3/4". On film, Villari looks like a fluid athlete. At his Pro Day, he didn't test in any of the explosive/strength drills, vertical, broad jump, or bench press. Bit of a discrepancy in the reporting of his forty yard dash times, RAS reports 4.77 with a 1.66 10-yard split, while others put him at a hand-timed 4.60. A 7.04 3cone shows stellar agility and flexibility. Burst and balance were excellent as well, 4.31 shuttle.

College film shows, even with his lack of experience, the looks of a natural fit at tight end. Primarily lined up in the slot, he gets to his spot and gives his quarterback a nice square target. Nice feel for open space. I have to describe his hands as iron in velvet, soft because the football just seems to be absorbed into his grip and strong because he plucks passes with his hands away from his body and tucks them away quickly. Solid wingspan and body control to haul in awry balls. Fearless over the middle and catches well through contact. As an open-field runner, I'd use "competitive" as the descriptor, he gets north/south in a hurry and runs low behind his pads, often right through first contact, Blocking needs a lot of technique and strength work. He's willing, but doesn't have much pop in his strikes and lacks the needed handwork/arm extension.

Came into the pros as a developmental prospect, but you can see he has the base traits. Villari has been on the receiving end of passes just three short years. He offers interesting versatility, although it would be highly suspect if the Rams would build a package of plays around an undrafted player joining the team this late in proceedings. He did however, run the ball out of wildcat formation, throws pretty well, and has very good hands. Like almost all youngsters, he needs route-running polish, but Villari's short area agility and natural move skills hint that he can handle a bigger route tree. Most of his targets were of the simpler variety, pivots, look-in/curls, and up the seams. In actuality, the current L.A. tight ends don't appear to be running a particularly complicated route tree either.

The Rams preseason lack of urgency in adding wide receiver depth hinted they're were going to make use of tight ends in the slot akin to receivers as a regular part of the rotation. Things have since changed due to all the injuries. Of the remaining two fully-available tight ends remaining, Parkinson can, and has been split out, but he's a bit heavy-footed and best suited closer to the action, while Max Klare is more natural to the slot, in skills, size, and athletically. Villari game appears more apt to fit in with Klare's.

Circumstances have certainly conspired against the Rams ball catchers, both wide outs and tight ends. Sean McVay would really be up against it if he were to try shapeshifting the offense again, back into three wide receiver sets. There doesn't appear to be many answers there. The L.A. braintrust looks limited in their options. At tight end, they will likely need to add a body. It could be a street retread or giving Villari a shot.

At $45k guaranteed, Villari was the Rams highest paid undrafted rookie in 2026, there must be more than "roster filler" interest, Yes indeed, he joined the team needing development and strength/conditioning work, but he's now been in the program for seven months, working on strength, technique and getting a grasp off the playbook. There is likely little or no upgrade available at this point.

In theory, McVay and tight ends coach Scott Huff could kick the tires on Villari, he has three practice squad elevations to the active roster, before a permanent decision needs to be made on his future. Elevated or signed, the Rams need to activate Dan Villari.

#2674. It’s time for Basketball: San Antonio Spurs vs Los Angeles Lakers

Welcome to the Game Thread. Veterans of the Game Thread know how we do things around here, but for all you newbies we have a few rules. Our community guidelines apply and basically say be cool, no personal attacks, don't troll and don't swear too much.

The Spurs lost their first road game and NBA Cup game of the season on Wednesday night, in a 111-106 thriller in front of an enthusiastic Moda Center crowd as both Dame and Deni Avdija went nuclear and out-executed the Silver and Black down the final stretch. Some missed free throws, a lane violation and an 8 second violation were costly as the Spurs ran the gamut of rarely enforced reasons to lose points at a key juncture of the game. The Spurs missed having De'Aaron Fox available, as his quickness and steady administration of the offensive sets was missed, especially in crunch time. Dylan Harper's absence was apparent, too, with the Spurs were missing his ability to get points even when the offense was not creating any space. The Spurs became too reliant on three point shooting, which isn't good for them, because only Champagnie is a good three-point shooter among the rotation players, and everybody in the Moda Center knew that, especially the Trail Blazer defenders. The good news is that Fox should be back in tonight's lineup. The better news is that Harper is listed as questionable on the injury report, which means that he could return to play tonight, just 10 days since fell on the court and injured his hip with less than a minute left in the Pistons game. Harper's injury was initially estimated to keep him out from 1-3 weeks (or 2-3 weeks, depending on where you read the news) and he's definitely on the lower end of that estimate.

Tonight, they face the Los Angeles Lakers in their final game of the Emirates Cup group stage. The math is pretty simple. In order to advance to the knockout rounds, they will have to beat the Lakers tonight. Because the Trail Blazers won on Wednesday, they will win the group and automatically advance if they win tonight's game against the Warriors, which tips off at the same time as the Lakers/Spurs game. In that case, a win for the Silver and Black would send them to the quarterfinals as the group winners, with a home game on December 4 or 5. If the Blazers win tonight, then the Spurs would probably advance to the semis as the Western Conference wild card, because they would have the best point differential among the second place finishers, barring some unlikely scenarios like the Grizzlies defeating the Timberwolves by 40+ or the Nuggets routing the Jazz by 50+ [OK, the second one could happen]. If the Spurs are the wild card, they will play on the road against the top team in the west, which would probably be the Wolves or Mavericks.

Is that all clear? Probably not. But if the Spurs lose tonight, it's even simpler. They will join the also-rans and have two more games added to the schedule in the second week of December against other non-qualifying teams. Although it's probably marginally better for the Spurs overall record, having two games against mediocre opponents added to the schedule than having to play two teams against top four teams in the conference, it would be a disappointment to a team that's looking to prove that they're ready to compete for the NBA title again this season. Last year, the top two teams in the NBA Cup were the teams in the NBA Finals, and that could happen again this season.

A lot of times, you can refer to the best player on the opponents' team as "the head of the snake." That's not exactly true of Luka Doncic. He's not the head of the snake, he's the whole damn snake. His usage rate is insanely high, and the rest of the team is pretty much relegated to watching him work on the offensive end. If the Spurs can force him to give up the ball early, and make the Lakers run the offense through someone else, especially if it's not Austin Reaves [questionable with a bruised heel], then the Spurs can hold down their scoring. The Lakers defense is decent, but the Spurs offense will be fine if they move the ball and don't just settle for three point shots. Let's GO SPURS!! Castle must dominate Luka.

#2672. Browns Announce 4-Year Extension With Key Starter

CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns scrambles while under pressure from defensive end Will Anderson Jr. #51 of the Houston Texans during the third quarter at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) Getty

CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. The Browns defeated the Texans 27-24. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) Getty

The Cleveland Browns locked in a key member of their special teams unit for the foreseeable future, announcing an extension on Friday.

The Browns signed long snapper Rex Sunahara to a four-year contract extension Friday, keeping him with the team through 2030.

"This is a cool moment for Rex as well as our organization because his journey is as blue collar as they come," general manager Andrew Berry said in a statement. "We're excited to extend him and make him a core part of our special teams operation moving forward."

Sunahara has played 39 games for Cleveland since his NFL debut in 2024. He's handled the snaps on all three of Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goals this season.

"It's a dream come true. There's no place I'd rather be," Sunahara said in the team's announcement.

GettyBrowns quarterback Deshaun Watson is playing for his future this season.

Most of the extension talk in Cleveland has centered on quarterback Deshaun Watson. He has seven regular-season games left on the fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract he signed in 2022.

Watson missed all of last season after tearing his Achilles tendon a second time. This year, he has led the winning drive in all six Cleveland victories. In his last start before the bye, he threw for 312 yards and ran for a team-high 49 more as the Browns erased a 17-point deficit to beat the Houston Texans 27-24.

Asked during the bye whether he wanted to stay in Cleveland, Watson said, "Yeah, of course." He left the question of negotiations to his agent, David Mulugheta.

My future — what that holds — is all in God's hands," Watson said. "Right now it's about playing good football, winning games, enjoying this moment because it can all be taken away. Right now I'm focusing on today, this bye week and finishing out the season strong.

"I want to continue to build on the legacy I'm building. Ultimately, it's up to the front office. It's up to Jimmy and Dee (Haslam), it's up to (Andrew Berry), it's up to coach Monken and the city. At the end of the day, all I can do is continue to play good football, win games and let them figure out what they want to do for the future."

Cleveland plans to wait until the season plays out before deciding whether to bring him back, according to Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot.

GettyThe Browns are set to host the Raiders for Sunday Night Football.

The next look at Watson will come on national television. The NFL flexed Cleveland's Nov. 29 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders to Sunday Night Football. It will be the first time since 2019 that the Browns have played host for SNF.

Cleveland comes out of the bye at 6-4, with a chance to start 5-0 at home. Each of those first four home wins took a go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter.

Cleveland's other prime-time game this season came down to a field goal. With the score tied against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Oct. 1, Sunahara snapped, Corey Bojorquez held and Szmyt hit a career-long 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left for a 27-24 win.

#2670. Aaron Rodgers: Sanctity of the locker room doesn't protect the coach from accountability

With Al Michaels calling today’s game in Pittsburgh, ex-Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers texted Michaels to give his side of the nasty breakup he just had with the team and head coach Mike McCarthy.

During the fourth quarter of the Broncos-Steelers game, Michaels read a text from Rodgers, in which Rodgers claimed he in no way violated the sanctity of the Steelers’ locker room when he went on Pat McAfee’s show to detail his problems with McCarthy.

“A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room,” Rodgers said in the text Michaels read during the game. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.”

Rodgers told McAfee that McCarthy, among other issues, wasn’t watching enough film, was sleeping in team meetings, and addressed the team as the “Packers” instead of the Steelers during halftime on Sunday.

McCarthy’s Steelers are dominating the Broncos today, which stands as a rebuke to Rodgers’ claim that McCarthy isn’t fit to be the team’s coach. But Rodgers was able to get his side of the story into the game, via his text to Michaels.

#2669. Victor Wembanyama makes MVP statement in Spurs' comeback win over Lakers

The roars of Frost Bank Center in the closing moments of the San Antonio Spurs' 99-96 win over the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday, Nov. 27 could've applied to two players on the floor at the time. After all, that's been the biggest debate of this young NBA season -- who between Victor Wembanyama and Luka Dončić is more of the favorite to be the league's Most Valuable Player five months from now?

But there was no mistaking who was the recipient of those chants on Friday. Spurs fans were going crazy for one of their own as Wembanyama capped off a 20-point comeback with a free throw to secure a 99-96 win over the Lakers, a spot in the NBA Cup quarterfinals and early bragging rights over Dončić.

It wasn't a bad night for the Lakers superstar; he finished the night with 31 points, six rebounds and eight assists. Nineteen of those points came in the first half as LA took a 16-point lead into the locker room. But once the teams came back out for the third quarter, it was all San Antonio.

The Lakers were outscored 61-42 by the Spurs over the last two quarters, powered by Wemby's 24 points, 16 rebounds and six stocks and 26 points from Stephon Castle.

"We just said we gotta find our energy, be on our front foot, which we weren't in the first half," Wembanyama said on NBA Nightcap postgame. "... New challenges every time, every season. We handled that one the right way."

The clash of MVP frontrunners lived up to its billing on Friday. So did the game's overall billing as the game of the year so far.

It was the two best teams in the Western Conference, with the two best players, with their supporting casts at full strength after Austin Reaves, Dylan Harper and De'Aaron Fox all returned from injuries. And for the Lakers, it answered a much-debated litmus test in regard to their strength of schedule. It's one thing to get to the top of the West by beating up on the Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazzes of the league, but the Lakers showed they can hang with – and at times look dominant against – the defending Western Conference champions.

This game was winnable for the Lakers, which makes the loss and the 17 turnovers all that much more frustrating. Things don't get any easier from here, however. They'll continue their road trip on Sunday against the No. 3-seeded Memphis Grizzlies before heading straight to Houston for the second night of a back-to-back against the fourth-place Rockets.

The Spurs will take on a slate of Eastern Conference opponents in the Boston Celtics, Milwaukee Brewers and Toronto Raptors before facing the Dallas Mavericks in the NBA Cup quarterfinals on Friday, Dec. 4.

USA TODAY Sports had you covered on live updates throughout the season's first meeting between two classic West rivals and two of the best players in the NBA. See more below:

The Lakers rallied at the end, but ran out of possessions as Mitch Johnson smartly had the Spurs foul down the stretch to prevent LA from having a chance to get the three they needed to force overtime in the closing seconds. The Spurs clinch their spot in the NBA Cup quarterfinals and supersede the Lakers for the top spot in the Western Conference.

The battle of MVP frontrunners was as advertised; Victor Wembanyama bounced back from a frustrating first half and finished the night with 25 points, 16 rebounds and six stocks while Luka Dončić scored 31 with six rebounds and eight assists.

The Lakers can't buy a bucket right now. The Spurs have open up an eight-point lead – their largest of the night – midway through the fourth after outscoring LA 13-5 since the end of the third. The Lakers have not made a field goal in almost two minutes; in that span, they've turned the ball over three times.

The Spurs have come alive in the second half. It was a chaotic third quarter with sloppy turnovers on both sides, but it's been San Antonio who had the upper hand, outscoring LA 30-14. They came out the gate on a 9-0 run that snatched the momentum in the early minutes to cut into the Lakers' 16-point halftime lead. Luka Dončić has 25 points but the Lakers as a whole missed 10 of their last 11 shots down the final stretch.

Victor Wembanyama jammed home the putback on a missed free throw from De'Aaron Fox to cut the Laker lead down to five at the 2:05 mark. Fox later hit a floater with 38 seconds left, and a three from Keldon Johnson knotted the game up at 68-all, erasing LA's lead heading into the fourth quarter.

Complete domination by LA in the first half. Luka Dončić has a game-high 19 points and is scoring almost at will to go along with five rebounds and three assists. And while Victor Wembanyama has been limited offensively due to head coach JJ Redick's clear gameplan of keying in on the 7'6 big man, but he still has five rebounds and four stocks (steals and blocks combined into one stat) with eight points.

In other Group C news, the Portland Trail Blazers lead the Golden State Warriors 67-44 at halftime. If both these scores hold, the Lakers will clinch the group and advance to the NBA Cup knockout rounds.

Reaves has struggled early in his first game back, missing each of his three attempts taken in the first quarter. So it's only fitting that his first points in the last five games came on a ridiculously tough shot.

Towards the end of the second quarter, Reaves dribbled out to the wing to avoid a one-on-one with Victor Wembanyama. When Devin Vassell switched onto him, Reaves immediately slashed to his left towards the paint and into the low post, stepped back and let it fly as he faded away with Wembanyama helping back late.

The ball swished through the net to give the Lakers a 19-point lead over the Spurs.

LA has gotten off to an early lead by forcing chaos in the paint, doubling Victor Wembanyama and forcing six Spurs turnovers. Luka Dončić is leading the way with 14 points for the Lakers on 6 of 13 shooting, though he's yet to hit a three in six attempts. Austin Reaves is still searching for his first points in his return to action.

#2668. Warriors, Yaxel Lendeborg can't find starting burst or closing edge in loss to Portland

PORTLAND, Ore. - They had survived, long enough. Impressively. Inexplicably. Hanging in, as Yaxel Lendeborg's legs hung in criss-cross at the scorer's table, a towel draped over his head. But play didn't stop, and so Steve Kerr burned a timeout - with his Golden State Warriors just about to get into an offensive set - simply to sub in Lendeborg, down 12 with six minutes left.

Golden State, simply and indefatigably, needed a closer. They Warriors had scrapped this hard, all the way back from a self-created 36-point second-quarter chasm. So Kerr went to the bullpen for the kid he'd bought three precious fourth-quarter minutes of rest for, the closer - the rookie - who needed, more than ever, to somehow tug on a Superman cape.

That cape has been missing, though, since Stephen Curry walked off the floor in Houston with an oblique injury earlier in November. These Warriors won't have him for at least two more games, possibly more. And two games of promising offensive adjustments fell utterly flat at the start and then at the end of a 116-94 loss to Portland, a disgusting sandwich around the meat of an attempted comeback.

After Lendeborg was subbed back, the Warriors scored just once - a Lendeborg layup - in more than five subsequent minutes of clock. The rookie had little left, bending over during one break in action with hands on knees. Guards De'Anthony Melton and Brandin Podziemski couldn't create offense. And roster issues again reared their ugly head, in a terrible start and a sad finish.

Quickly, by the first few minutes of the second quarter, Lendeborg could do no more than simply chuck the ball at the stanchion. He didn't put much velocity on it. That would've signaled anger. This was a toss of frustration. A toss of exasperation. A toss like a kid chucking his remote from the couch after trying, and failing, to beat a boss level on a video game for 15 minutes.

3-Point Goals: 14-42, .333 (Melton 5-10, Podziemski 3-7, Horford 2-5, Santos 1-1, Payton II 1-2, Williams 1-2, Lendeborg 1-4, Cryer 0-2, Niang 0-2, Green 0-3, Richard 0-4).

Blocked Shots: 6 (Lendeborg 2, Green, Horford, Payton II, Podziemski).

Turnovers: 16 (Melton 5, Bassey 3, Green 2, Lendeborg, Niang, Payton II, Podziemski, Santos, Williams).

Steals: 8 (Melton 2, Green, Horford, Lendeborg, Payton II, Podziemski, Santos).

3-Point Goals: 12-49, .245 (Camara 4-8, Holiday 2-5, Potter 2-5, Henderson 2-9, Clingan 1-5, Kent 1-5, Carlson 0-1, Cissoko 0-5, Avdija 0-6).

Blocked Shots: 6 (Clingan 3, Holiday, Potter, Williams III).

Turnovers: 11 (Avdija 5, Cissoko 2, Holiday 2, Clingan, Williams III).

Steals: 8 (Avdija 2, Camara 2, Cissoko, Henderson, Holiday, Potter).

The onslaught had continued here, early in the second quarter at the Moda Center, as Blazers reserve Micah Potter finished a putback layup through contact. Micah Potter. Do you know who Micah Potter is? You'd be forgiven, if not. He went undrafted in 2021, and entered Friday night's game averaging 2.2 points per game.

The Warriors made him look like prime Kevin Love for several minutes, this first half, as the game-to-game cracks in this roster's foundation only widen each passing matchup without Curry. They eked out a win over Boston, sure, because they out-scrapped and out-hustled a visibly fatigued and scuffling Celtics group. On Wednesday, they blitzed the Kings, a franchise that's looked completely lost. And they'd believed they'd found something offensively by inserting Charles Bassey at center and shifting Draymond Green back to power forward, placing the ball back in Green's hands more often and thereby re-driving his offensive impact with Curry sidelined.

"He's more involved as the four-man than he was as the five, in a lot of different ways," Kerr said pregame. "And I think he's feeling like he's being utilized more, and it's good for his confidence, and just his overall engagement in the game."

Friday night in Portland, though, was the true test. The Trail Blazers have established themselves as an early Western Conference contender, and with star guards Damian Lillard and Ja Morant out, started Deni Avdija - all 6-foot-8 of him - at the shooting guard. They are long. They are mean. They tossed two of the best perimeter defenders in the league, in Jrue Holiday and Toumani Camara, at a Golden State team with no true lead ballhandler in its starting lineup.

Kerr can only do so much with this current group, where Melton and Podziemski aren't true point guards and backup Brandon Williams is shaking off rust from a hamstring injury. The Blazers, Kerr hinted pregame, would be a challenge.

"I think we're finding our rhythm offensively, since, the trip, where we really struggled," Kerr said. "But this (Portland) team - it's a different animal defensively. They're gonna test us way more than the last couple games felt. So we're going to feel that pressure. We gotta see how we can respond to it."

They folded, early, in a perfect storm of a Portland team geared to exploit Golden State's size and length deficits and a Warriors team that has resoundingly and only semi-explicably become one of the worst first-quarter teams on the road in the NBA. They hung 14 points in the first frame in San Antonio two weeks ago, and then 11 in New Orleans, and subsequently went down 25-9 to Dallas, and no offensive tweaks could save them here in Portland: out-physicaled by Portland bigs Donovan Clingan and Robert Williams III and outrun by Avdija in transition and simply outmatched in a gruesome 47-11 deficit to start.

More than any night, even after a previous five-game losing streak, this matchup in Portland exposed the Warriors' lack of a non-Curry initiator. Melton, despite catching fire again with five triples, finished the night with five gruesome turnovers. Podziemski only picked up pick-and-roll momentum in the second half. Lendeborg spent much of the first half playing off-ball - until Golden State opted to again run the offense through their 24-year-old beacon of hope in the second half, and results followed.

He took off in transition in the third, shaking Holiday on a behind-the-back and soaring to flush an and-one jam on Holiday's head. He nailed a stepback triple from the corner later in the period, clutching his fists and roaring. He put his head down and bull-rushed at the heart of Portland-red jerseys until he heard a whistle. He had 14 second-half points, and suddenly the Warriors threatened down 10 with five minutes left.

It wasn't enough. That second-quarter chasm was too severe.

#2667. Steelers credit T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward for leadership amidst adverse week

The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to a very adverse week by dominating the Denver Broncos 27-5 to get to 7-4 and remain unbeaten at home in 2026.

It was a trying week for the Steelers, who released quarterback Aaron Rodgers after he demanded to take over play-calling duties. Rodgers then went on The Pat McAfee Show and put head coach Mike McCarthy on blast for falling asleepp in meetings, missing walk throughs, and not getting to know defensive players, among other things.

In trying times like this, teams lean on their leaders, and several players credited T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward for the work they did with the team this week.

"I thought TJ and Cam did a really good job before the game," Pat Freiermuth said via Brooke Pryor. "Really talking about it's bigger than one person, it's bigger than two people… It's about the Rooney family and the Steelers and the fans, and they deserve our best effort today."

Safety Jaquan Brisker echoed those sentiments.

"We had a very important leadership council meeting this week, and we all were in there and talked about keeping this team together and turning the page," Brisker said via Nick Farabaugh.

Quarterback Mason Rudolph, who threw a touchdown pass in the win, pointed out how lucky the Steelers are to have superstars with high leadership abilities.

"Your average team doesn't have a Cam Heyward or a T.J. Watt or a Jalen Ramsey," Rudolph said. "Those guys did an awesome job at just pointing the trajectory of where the team needed to go.

Pittsburgh took a bunch of cannonball shots this week, but it's clear their foundation is strong due to the leaders they have inside their locker room. They will now get ready for a Week 13 matchup with the Houston Texans next week on Sunday Night Football.

#2666. Vecino, dalla Fiorentina alla Lazio: Sarri e la seconda giovinezza

Il centrocampista ripercorre i prestiti a Cagliari ed Empoli e ricorda il derby vinto e il gol di Provedel.

Matias Vecino ripercorre il cammino dalla Fiorentina alla Lazio: i prestiti a Cagliari ed Empoli, il lavoro con Maurizio Sarri e quella che definisce una «seconda giovinezza» in biancoceleste. Secondo quanto riportato da Gianlucadimarzio, Dopo tredici anni di calcio italiano, tra esperienze, incontri e traguardi, il centrocampista è in attesa di un nuovo capitolo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Intervistato da Gianlucadimarzio.com, Vecino parte dal suo arrivo dall’Uruguay nel 2013. Aveva grandi aspettative, ma anche qualche timore per ciò che avrebbe trovato in Italia.

«È stato un salto molto grande», racconta Vecino. «Da un lato ero felicissimo, dall’altro avevo un po’ di ansia perché non sapevo cosa avrei trovato.» L’inserimento fu più semplice di quanto immaginasse grazie ai compagni e alle persone che lavoravano nel club. Tra coloro che lo aiutarono ricorda Borja Valero, Gonzalo Rodriguez e Neto: era ancora un ragazzo, con molto da imparare.

Il debutto in Italia arrivò il 26 settembre 2013, a San Siro, durante Inter-Fiorentina. Era già stato in panchina nelle partite precedenti, senza entrare in campo. L’emozione coinvolse anche la sua famiglia, che lo seguiva dall’Uruguay. Giocare in quello stadio contro calciatori come Cambiasso e Milito gli diede la sensazione di essere un giocatore vero. Durante l’azione restava concentrato, ma quando il pallone usciva poteva guardarsi attorno e sentire l’importanza del momento.

Per trovare spazio in Serie A, Vecino passò in prestito al Cagliari e all’Empoli. Alla Fiorentina giocava in una squadra importante, ma le occasioni erano limitate: considera quelle due esperienze una scelta giusta per accumulare minuti.

In Sardegna trovò Diego Lopez, uruguaiano come lui, in una squadra che aveva bisogno di una mezzala. A Empoli lavorò con Sarri, in un gruppo con molti giovani. Ricorda un campionato in cui la squadra giocò molto bene e si divertì, in un ambiente familiare. Fu la sua prima stagione intera da titolare: «tatticamente mi ha migliorato al 100%», dice a proposito del tecnico.

Dopo due anni in prestito tornò alla Fiorentina, con cui raccolse 78 presenze in due anni. Tornare in viola era sempre stato il suo obiettivo: il club lo aveva preso dall’Uruguay e aspettato, e lui desiderava costruirvi un percorso lungo. Il rientro coincise con l’arrivo di Paulo Sousa. Vecino ricorda una squadra forte nel primo anno e il divertimento dei tifosi, ma ritiene che alla lunga abbia pesato l’impegno in Europa League.

#2665. 49ers announce Mac Jones will start vs. Seahawks, Brock Purdy is out

Mac Jones will start at quarterback for the 49ers on Sunday against the Seahawks.

Brock Purdy, who is an MVP candidate this season, has not practiced all week with an ankle injury, and on Friday, head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that Purdy has been ruled out. Shanahan said Jones is ready to go and will play well on Sunday.

“Mac’s been awesome,” Shanahan said. “He’s had a great week. We went through this with him last year so everyone’s got a ton of confidence in Mac. Mac’s had a hell of a camp and he’s the same guy every day. It’s been a good week with Mac.”

Last year Jones started eight games while Purdy was hurt, and although Jones didn’t play as well as Purdy, he did play well enough for the 49ers to go 5-3 in those eight games.

Now the 49ers will hope Jones can play well enough to beat the defending Super Bowl champions in a game that has major implications for the NFC playoff race.

#2664. Who’s got Cup fever?! Sixers dominate Pacers, win Group B, advance to knockout stage

The Cup continues to bring the best out of the game's greatest.

The Sixers handled the Indiana Pacers 111-87 Friday night. They advance to the Knockout Stage of the NBA Cup for the first time as a franchise, winning Eastern Conference Group B. They're next Cup game will be either Dec. 4 or 5.

LeBron James kept his hot hand, finishing with 21 points, seven rebounds and six assists shooting 8-of-13 from the floor. VJ Edgecombe went for nine points on 4-of-6 shooting along with five rebounds and seven assists.

Tyrese Maxey struggled from the field, shooting 3-of-13 for 13 points, but did also have six assists. Returning from a two-game absence due to illness, Joel Embiid had some rust to shake off, going 5-of-14 from the floor to finish with 14 points along with 11 boards.

Jaylen Brown was once again out for the Sixers with hamstring injury management, as was Dean Wade. Tyrese Haliburton and T.J. McConnell were out for Indiana.

This game started as ideally as it could for the Sixers. The fifth starter for the night was Dominick Barlow, who opened the scoring by cutting to the basket for an easy layup. LeBron buried a couple of threes, one just beat the shotclock with a hand in his face, before Barlow put back a Maxey miss to start the game on a 10-2 Sixers run. LeBron drilled his third attempt following a Pacer timeout but missed his heat check on the following possession.

There was a lot of violence at the rim early as Embiid tried to dunk on Kelly Oubre Jr. as he got open on a roll, but Oubre stuffed the attempt and gave a hearty celebration after. Trying to get down the floor quickly, the Pacers turned it over with a sloppy pass, as Maxey was able to get the ball out to Edgecombe who threw it down hard.

The center substitutions were very frequent early. Embiid's first shift was under five minutes. Adem Bona played for just 2:41 and made an impact in that time, pinning an Aaron Nesmith attempt against the backboard. Indiana opened the game 3-of-12 from the floor as a team.

It was good to see Labaron Philon Jr. back in the mix, but the Embiid-plus-bench lineup did not get off to a good start. Embiid allowed Jay Huff to swoop into the lane for an offensive rebound, turning that into a corner three. The Sixers called timeout, but were unable to stop the run as Jabari Walker got called for an offensive foul coming out of it. Nesmith got to the line to cap off a 9-0 Pacers push. Embiid knocked down a three and Simons put up a quick five to keep the Sixers up by eight after the first.

The Sixers' offense slowed down, taking nearly three minutes to score their first points of the second. It was another impressive LeBron bucket as he banked home a layup despite still trying to get his hands on Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's pass, but Indy kept creeping back on the other end.

Edgecombe hit a big three off an offensive rebound which forced a Pacer timeout, but the offense was still struggling to get back on track. Maxey didn't score his first points until halfway through the quarter, starting 0-of-3 with three turnovers.

It does seem like luck snow piles when your shot isn't falling. The offense had broken down into a lot of isolations, but Maxey also had a very open floater in the paint rim halfway down and out. On the next possession he took a deep, early three in the shotclock which also bounced around before falling out.

Nick Nurse called a timeout after the Pacers had cut the lead to one and was able to draw up something to get them out of the funk. A few screens got Walker an open corner three that he nailed. Embiid and Maxey went to their two-man game on the next two possessions, getting an elbow jumper for the former and a layup for the latter.

The Sixers had plenty of time to get their act together thanks to the Pacers shooting 2-of-17 from behind the arc in the first half. They got to the free throw line way more than the Sixers, but they would have been able to take a lead had they hit anything from outside. Ironically, it looked like their third of the night was falling right before the half, but Ivica Zubac got called for basket interference. That gave Maxey time for one more drive, getting to the line to give the Sixers an 11-point lead at the half.

Barlow's impact was felt inside when he was on the floor. He picked up his second block early in the third. A couple possessions after he did that, he grabbed a missed Embiid jumper and dunked it back over the head of a defender.

Offensively the Sixers got some easy stuff to start the half. Maxey and LeBron each got to the line and LeBron bully balled his way for an easy post-up. They got a little jumper-happy again once they got the lead up to 18 and went cold on their pull-ups. A nice cut from Barlow was rewarded by James to break that up and prompt another Pacers timeout.

Bona struggled a bit more in his quick third quarter shift, picking up his third and fourth fouls in about a 30-second span. The Sixers seemed to have even more leeway to mess around though. Just like how they shot from the first half from three, the Pacers opened the third quarter 2-of-17 from the field.

In 59 seconds of game time Simons hit as many threes as the Pacers had all night. He started it with a stepback off the dribble over his defender. After a timeout, he came off a screen for his second and hit another pull-up for his third. Maxey hit him with a crosscourt pass a few possessions later for another before he missed his heatcheck several feet behind the arc as the Sixers coasted to a 27-point lead.

Despite some other games making it not really matter, the Sixers were fighting for that point differential to start the third. KCP got on the board with a couple of baskets, Barlow picked up a couple more cutting layups, and Simons hit a running layup.

Philon might have checked back into the game a little later in the second half than some may have wanted, but it was nice to see him drill a three as well. The end of the bench did allow a quick 9-0 run that prompted an angry timeout from Nurse after a Philon turnover.

The Sixers' scoring drought that lasted over three and a half minutes was ended by Tacko Fall, who got a big round of cheers from the fans left in the arena upon doing so. Fall was able to front Huff and slam home a big dunk on the next possession to give the people what they wanted to see.

#2661. Steelers players express support for Mike McCarthy after winning first game since Aaron Rodgers divorce

It can't be denied the Pittsburgh Steelers are a different team after one of the most eventful weeks of the season, but that apparently isn't all bad.

A number of Steelers players expressed their support for head coach Mike McCarthy in the aftermath of a 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, the team's first game since a very public divorce with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

The saga saw Rodgers make several claims while appearing on "The Pat McAfee Show" that painted McCarthy as disconnected at best and dangerously incompetent at worst after the Steelers benched him, and shortly before they released him. It's a situation with a little precedent in the NFL, and it led to all eyes on McCarthy and the Steelers in Week 12.

Behind the scenes, there was plenty of talking. James Palmer of NFL Network reported before the game that the team's leadership council — a group of veteran players who regularly meet with McCarthy — met on Wednesday and held an "airing of grievances" to address some of the stuff Rodgers was talking about. The meeting reportedly left McCarthy "humbled," but also allowed him to explain to the players why he handled everything the way he did.

The meeting apparently left the team on firmer footing, with Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey saying the team expressed its support to McCarthy:

"For the past couple days, we as players, we were like, 'Coach, you good.' Let us turn this up, let us get in our zone."

Quarterback Mason Rudolph, Rodgers' replacement under center, also said the players were behind McCarthy:

"I think the leadership council rallied around coach McCarthy. I think in a weird way, the adversity probably brought us closer together. We've just got to keep carrying that in week to week."

McCarthy, meanwhile, seemed happy with how the team responded:

"Everything that was discussed was healthy. Lot of things in there, but what came out of it was urgency. I thought our leaders did a tremendous job of bringing the urgency to their rooms and it definitely showed up."

One particular point of criticism from Rodgers was that McCarthy had allegedly spent little time engaging with the Pittsburgh defense, despite the quarterback advising that he should. McCarthy's background is almost purely on the offense and he's well known to prioritize that side of the ball while leaving the rest to his defensive coordinator.

McCarthy actually admitted Rodgers was right about his lack of focus on the defense:

"I have not spent enough time with the defense. That's something as far as job responsibility, job description, these are things that will be looked at in the offseason, but it's a point where in our year, we're making adjustments. Definitely conscientious of it."

Steelers defensive end T.J. Watt indicated the players spoke to McCarthy about that, and the results were encouraging:

"Mike just admitted that he has got to spend some more time with the defense. We've had a lot of really good conversations, especially recently, and look forward to continuing to build off of what you saw tonight."

Mike McCarthy had a tough week, but got a win.

The Steelers veterans also had plenty of praise for Rudolph, whose experience with the team goes back to 2018. Watt didn't seem surprised he was ready for the game:

"Mason Rudolph is a true professional. He's been a true professional since I've known him. A guy that's trained like the starter no matter how long he's been here, whether he's the backup or the starter. We have extreme belief in him and he's a great locker room glue guy."

Rudolph didn't exactly light up the scoreboard against Denver, but he was at least efficient, going 9-for-15 for 142 yards, 1 touchdown and 0 interceptions. It was a run-heavy game script with the Steelers leading 14-0 after the first quarter and by multiple scores for the rest of the game.

Still, Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward noticed Rudolph doing what was needed:

"He's ready for all those moments. He understand that with everything that went on, he couldn't have a drop-off. I'm just appreciative to have a guy who when s*** hits the fan, he's able to say, 'Alright, I've gotta step up.'"

It was a strong performance at least compared to, well, the standard Rodgers set during the season. NFL Network's Michael Florio noted his 0.19 EPA per dropback, an advanced stat measuring offensive efficiency, was the second-best mark by a Steelers quarterback all season. Rodgers exceeded that level only once all season, in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals.

McCarthy did at one point go out of his way to note "I'm the offensive play-caller," a notable statement given that Rodgers reportedly gave the Steelers an ultimatum that the team give him offensive play-calling duties or release him.

However, he seemed far more interested in moving on with the team as constructed, and said he was grateful for the response to a turbulent week:

"There's a lot going on. Anytime you're in a situation where time is taken away from winning and your team responds, it is extremely important and gratifying. The reality of this game — and it will always be as far as my approach — this is a players' game. We have a very important role in this sport, but you have to make sure you keep it about the players. We still have work to do from my position and we'll continue to do that. We've just got to keep building off things that we've done well.

"We got the win today. It was definitely a hard travel week for us as a football team. I'm proud of our players. I'm proud of our coaching staff. I'm proud of our support staff and I really appreciate all the other support."

Meanwhile, Rodgers, passed along his own thoughts via Al Michaels during the game.
