#2654. The Raptors showed they can win tonight: even if it’s just the Nets

To borrow words from Bret Easton Ellis' American Psycho (1991), there is an idea of a Toronto Raptors, some kind of abstraction, but there is no real team, only what they look like on the floor that night. But against the Nets, the Raptors looked like the type of team that they've billed themselves as since last season. Big, dangerous, able to guard well, while hitting their shots inside and outside of the arc.

And tonight, with Collin Murray-Boyles, Scottie Barnes, and Allen Graves all playing solid minutes, it looked like Vision 6'9" come to life, like a monster animated with the sole purpose of clobbering the Brooklyn Nets.

The first quarter had the Raptors shooting — and more importantly, making — more threes than usual. They outshot the Nets by both accuracy and volume, with Barnes and Graves looking like a real one-two punch. Julius Randle, while delivering thundering dunks, went 0-3 from three in the first quarter, as the Raptors ran a solid transition offence. The Raptors left the first quarter up four points on the Nets, despite Brooklyn dominating in the painted area, scoring 16 of its 27 points there.

Raptors fought themselves into a double digit lead over the Nets with an Allen Graves three, and continued to build momentum as the second quarter wound down. Scottie Barnes took it to the rack with a spin move into a filthy left hander that left the room begging for more. The Nets heated up from three by the end of the second quarter, but the Raptors maintained their lead into halftime.

The third quarter saw Immanuel Quickley rain in treys, as the Raptors' lead continued to grow. They cracked 100 points as the seconds rolled down, up more than 20 points. At the end of the quarter, Barnes drove to the basket and laid it in, cracking 30 points with 12 minutes left in the game.

By then, Barnes had not grabbed a single rebound, with his teammates doing a lot of the dirty work down low. Further, while Scottie generated great looks, it was Quickley who picked up double digit points and assists in the contest. Against a bad team, Barnes was able to focus on scoring, anchoring the Raptors' offence as they blazed past the Nets. The idea central to the Raptors' building around Scottie had, for the past two seasons, been to pair the young forward with a more veteran scorer.

However, this season has allowed Barnes to prove that on a nightly basis, he can take the top defensive or offensive assignment for the team. Barnes' ability to switch has long been lauded, but the offensive versatility he has displayed is something that the Raptors would benefit from remembering when Kawhi Leonard returns.

The Brooklyn Nets are the Brooklyn Nets, and using a hot knife to cleave through butter isn't a good test to see if your knife is actually sharp. But, it's nice to see after the Milwaukee debacle that the Raptors still have it in them to stomp the NBA's bad teams. More than that, however, tonight showed a version of the Raptors with high highs and low lows, with much to be emulated, and some things to be firmly rejected.

TORONTO, CANADA – NOVEMBER 27: Julius Randle #30 of the Brooklyn Nets dunks against Collin Murray-Boyles #30 of the Toronto Raptors during the first half of the Emirates NBA Cup group stage game at Scotiabank Arena on November 27, 2026 in Toronto, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mark Blinch/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The shooting, especially from those who aren't usually snipers, was great. Allen Graves getting the minutes he needs to develop, and shining in them, produced some great highlights. But, moments of awkwardness, especially the Nets powering through the Raptors in the paint, were something that did not befit a team that projects a defensive mindset as outwardly as Toronto does.

While Ja'Kobe Walter was forced to leave the game with an injury, and did not return, he was quiet from the field, scoring his only points from the charity stripe. Similarly, Jaminson Battle ended the game with 1-6 from three. Sometimes, the shots just don't fall, but the Raptors shouldn't need to compromise between their shooters having good games from range.

Tonight's numbers from the Raptors looked great, but as much as the Raptors won this game, the Nets also lost it, giving up victory to the Raptors rather than having it taken from them forcibly. The rebounding difference between both teams is not something the Raptors will likely be able to sustain against more poised teams, nor the three point volume, but tonight's efficiency is what the team should model, and strive for, especially in harder matchups.

#2651. Brock Purdy ruled out vs. Seahawks. Can Mac Jones carry 49ers offense?

The San Francisco 49ers will be without their quarterback for the first of their two-game NFC West leg this week.

Brock Purdy has been ruled out for their Week 12 divisional matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, head coach Kyle Shanahan announced on Friday, Nov. 27. Mac Jones will get the start at home against the defending Super Bowl champions.

Purdy sprained his left ankle in the second quarter of the Mexico City game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 22, though he kept playing and finished with 255 passing yards and three touchdowns in a 35-10 win to push the Niners' NFL-best record to 9-1. He did not practice all week while nursing his ankle and despite Shanahan's optimism that he wouldn't miss time, Purdy is now being shut down for the week after it was revealed he suffered a mid-ankle sprain, which typically is slower to heal.

Shanahan told reporters Friday that Purdy won't require surgery. Does he expect his franchise QB back next week against the Los Angeles Rams?

"It's too soon, but I mean I'm pretty optimistic about it," he said. "But I was (optimistic) about this week to start and then it changes, so hopefully it'll be all right."

Without Purdy, the Niners have been in good hands with Jones, who went 5-3 in eight games started a year ago when Purdy went down with a toe injury. In those eight games, Jones threw 13 touchdowns for 2,151 yards with six interceptions and a 97.4 passer rating.

The Seahawks, on the other hand, are no stranger to quarterback injuries this year. They'll have Sam Darnold back on Sunday from a quad injury that kept him out of their last two games.

Though the 49ers are tied with the Chicago Bears for most wins in the league with nine, these next two divisional games against the third-place Seahawks and second-place Rams will be crucial as they lead LA by 2 1/2 games in the ultracompetitive NFC West.

#2650. Knicks have no late-game magic as they’re eliminated from NBA Cup title defense

Captain Clutch had a chance to tie the game with three free throws after Ryan Conwell's boneheaded foul on Brunson's corner 3-pointer with 9.8 seconds left. But Brunson's first free throw clanked off the rim — a rare shortcoming for him in a big moment.

Brunson made the next two, and the Knicks trailed by one. But they weren't able to foul on the subsequent Heat possession, as Pelle Larsson's dunk put Miami back up three with 7.2 seconds left. Brunson — while trying to draw another foul — missed a 3-pointer on the other end, and the Knicks' six-game winning streak came to an end as they fell 108-105 to the Heat on Friday night at Madison Square Garden.

Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo pulls down a rebound away from New York Knicks guard Josh Hart on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. JASON SZENES FOR NEW YORK POST

"Very," Brunson said when asked how frustrating it was to miss the free throw.

Friday's loss meant the Knicks were officially eliminated from the NBA Cup. They needed to win by at least seven points and get a Pacers win over the 76ers to advance. Neither happened.

Brunson's missed free throws came on the possession after James Wiseman similarly came up short from the line.

Trailing by two with 36.8 seconds left in the game, the Knicks needed a stop and seemed to have bottled up Giannis Antetokounmpo, who tried to throw the ball off the backboard to himself. But Karl-Anthony Towns fouled him on the play.

Antetokounmpo missed both free throws, however, and Bam Adebayo fouled Wiseman going for the rebound after the second miss. Wiseman could have tied the game with 12.5 seconds left by making both. He made the first, but his second free throw rimmed out.

So, the Knicks overcoming a 23-point deficit was all for naught.

New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson reacts to referee Scott Foster after a call at Madison Square Garden in New York, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. JASON SZENES FOR NEW YORK POST

"We did not have a great shootaround today with our focus," coach Mike Brown said. "We have to be better in our shootarounds, coming into games — especially games like this. It was evident with how sloppy we played."

There will be no defense of the Knicks' NBA Cup title. They didn't even make it to the knockout rounds after going 1-3 in the group stage.

But being eliminated could end up a blessing in disguise. Brown — even before his team was knocked out — said that this time around, he values the extra rest the Knicks will get by not advancing in the tournament. And with how banged up they are, he's probably right — the Knicks (12-7) were without OG Anunoby (left calf strain), Miles McBride (sports hernia), Jordan Clarkson (right plantar fasciitis) and Andre Drummond (concussion protocol) on Friday. Towns played but has been battling an abdominal ailment.

Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo pulls down a rebound away from New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, in New York. JASON SZENES FOR NEW YORK POST

Now the Knicks will get easier opponents (other teams who were eliminated) and play just two games — one home and one on the road — over a nine-day stretch in the beginning of December. Advancing would have meant better opposition (other teams who advanced) and the potential for up to three more road games if they reached the Final.

Friday was their first matchup against the Heat since Miami acquired Antetokounmpo over the offseason. And the Greek Freak delivered his first 20-20 game for the Heat with 22 points and 23 rebounds. Adebayo, his partner in crime in a dominant frontcourt, had 25 points and seven rebounds. Towns recorded his 19th straight double-double to start the season with 19 points and 10 rebounds, but he couldn't take on the Giannis-Bam duo by himself.

"One guy has the second-most points in a game ever and the other guy, he's an MVP, a former MVP," Towns said. "It goes back to execution."

Brunson had a game-high 27 points — but the Knicks needed 28 out of him.

The Heat like to utilize a zone defense with their dominant frontcourt and an elite perimeter defender in Davion Mitchell. And it gave the Knicks offense fits in the first half — they shot just 39.5 percent from the field across the first two quarters.

They were able to largely figure it out in the second half, but were let down by their end-of-game execution.

Last year, the Knicks' NBA Cup triumph was a precursor to their actual championship. They better hope this year's failed Cup run isn't a preview of anything else.

"Obviously disappointed we can't defend the Cup championship," Towns said. "But we still have a lot more games to get ourselves ready to defend the world championship."

#2649. How a football team rebuilt after 19 players died in plane crash

It was 2am when Ivan Tozzo picked up his mobile phone and heard his football club's secretary screaming his name.

A plane carrying the Chapecoense team had crashed into a mountain.

Seventy-one people were dead, including 19 of 22 players from the Brazilian club who were on their way to the biggest game in their history.

It would later emerge the plane had run out of fuel and investigators would find the airline and pilot were to blame as the fuel load was insufficient for the flight on 28 November 2016.

But in the early hours, as Tozzo watched the TV news in the changing room at the club's stadium, his only thought was for the players who would not be coming back to this room.

When he sat alone in the club's boardroom after the funerals as the only director still alive, he cried.

That was the moment when Tozzo – who had changed his mind about travelling with the team because he had a sense of unease about the trip - decided he would lead Chapecoense to rise again.

Ivan Tozzo recalls the phone call he got after the crash: "It was our club secretary, Jorilda, who was desperate, screaming 'Ivan Ivan'." [Getty Images]

Chapecoense had been travelling to Colombia to play Atletico Nacional of Medellin in the first leg of the Copa Sudamericana final, South America's second most prestigious club tournament.

It was a first continental final for the Brazilian team.

"The team was very motivated, knowing that we were engraving our names inside the history of the club," goalkeeper Jakson Follmann, one of the three surviving players, tells BBC Sport.

Aged 24 at the time, Follmann had also been looking forward to his imminent wedding, little knowing he would be spending two months in hospital instead.

"Everyone was completely proud of everything they were doing, both for the team and for the community of Chapeco and the region," Follmann says.

Commentator Rafael Henzel, who was one of six survivors of the crash but who died in 2019 following a heart attack, described the Copa Sudamericana as the team's "World Cup" and said in 2017 that "if anyone's ever died happy, it was the people on that plane".

The LaMia 2933 flight from Santa Cruz in Bolivia to the Colombian city of Medellin had a journey distance similar to the plane's flying range, but it did not stop to refuel and crashed into a mountain just 18km from its intended destination.

The pilot, Miguel Quiroga, who was also a co-owner of the airline, died in the crash. In a leaked tape, he can be heard warning of a "total electric failure" and "lack of fuel". However, he did not make a formal distress call.

A Bolivian investigation concluded that the pilot and the airline were directly responsible for the crash, while a Colombian investigation said there was no technical failure and blamed the pilot, the airline and Bolivian regulators.

"I don't call it an accident, I say it was a crime that could have been avoided," says Follman, whose right leg had to be partially amputated to save his life.

"It's the crime of not stopping to refuel, the greed to think that he [the pilot] could get there... with the fuel practically finished."

To date, no-one has been found guilty in relation to the crash.

At the time, Bolivia did not have a system for prosecuting companies. Even when such a facility was introduced in 2021, it did not cover negligent homicide or causing an air disaster.

Charges were brought against individuals in LaMia's management - who denied wrongdoing - but in 2020 a trial was delayed by jurisdictional disputes and difficulties involving defendants who were abroad.

The plane was just 18km from its destination when it ran out of fuel [Getty Images]

A number of key details about the disaster were established early on.

At 21:16 local time, the aircraft displayed a low fuel warning but flew on without the crew alerting local authorities.

Fourteen minutes later, the plane began its descent to Medellin airport but was put in a holding pattern.

At 21:49, the crew requested priority permission to land, vaguely citing "problems with fuel".

"I remember the lights went out suddenly; then I started praying, asking God to help us," recalled defender Neto, the last of the survivors to be found.

"But a lot of people thought the plane was just landing because it was not an abrupt fall."

Within five minutes, all the engines, drained of fuel, failed.

"Then, I couldn't hear the plane engine any more. It was just a wind. And then an alarm: beep beep beep," Neto told the BBC World Service in 2017.

Thousands of people gathered in the rain as the funeral cortege went past [Getty Images]

Seven thousand kilometres away in the small southern Brazilian city of Chapeco, Tozzo watched the scale of the disaster unfold on TV screens at the stadium in the middle of the night.

"At five o'clock in the morning, the players' wives began to arrive. It was despair. People threw themselves on the ground and cried," says Tozzo, a local entrepreneur who was the club's vice-president at the time and had joined the club in 2009 when they were not even playing in Brazil's national football pyramid.

Two days earlier, Tozzo had suffered misgivings about the trip that were so strong that he had changed his mind about travelling to Medellin.

"It was a thing from God. It was not for me to go. I called [financial director] Decio, who organised all our trips, and I told him that I would not go," he says.

"He went crazy with me. 'Why? You agreed to go, now you do not want to go? You have to go.'

"My sister was next to me, saying, 'You need to go to this match, you worked so hard to get to this moment.' But in my head I said, 'No Ivan, I will not go', and I stayed at home."

After the crash, he had another strong feeling about his path.

"I think I had a mission here on Earth to continue Chapecoense after the accident," Tozzo says. "I was the only one of the directors left alive so I took over as [interim] president."

A sleepless week followed in which Tozzo arranged flights to Colombia for doctors, relatives and pastors to identify and recover the remains and be with the survivors.

A memorial service was organised and, in pouring rain, the coffins were brought into Chape's stadium, Arena Conda.

During the service came the news that Atletico Nacional had asked for the Copa Sudamericana trophy and winners' prize money to be awarded to Chapecoense.

Tozzo was determined Chapecoense would compete again, but none of the surviving players were in any shape to play and they only had two other squad members – who did not travel to Medellin because of injury – and a handful in the academy.

They called on Rui Costa, who had been sacked by Gremio as football director six months earlier and accepted the same role with Chapecoense, and appointed Vagner Mancini as coach.

In a matter of weeks, 22 new players were signed, most of them on loan.

Tozzo's message rang clear in the ears of the new players.

"Our fans were very sad, Chapecoense was very sad, and playing again with joy was not easy," he says.

"We explained very well the responsibility they would have."

Chapecoense's new players line up for their first match [Getty Images]

Chapecoense's first match back – eight weeks after the crash – was a friendly against the last team the club had played, Palmeiras.

Before the game at the Arena Conda, Follmann – in a wheelchair – was joined by Neto and the other surviving player, Alan Ruschel, to receive the Copa Sudamericana trophy.

"It was the first time I had gone back to the arena, the first time I really had contact with people, because I was still hospitalised," says Follmann.

"When I received the trophy, a movie went through my head because our captain Cleber Santana should have been holding it surrounded by all of us, celebrating."

The friendly against Palmeiras was the first of 80 matches that Chapecoense played in 2017, only five of them friendlies.

There was an offer from the Brazilian Football Confederation to give the club immunity from relegation for three seasons, but Tozzo rejected it.

"How can you psych up the players to play their best if they know that their classification is guaranteed?" he asks.

As it turned out, Chapecoense stayed up on their own merits for precisely three seasons.

Chapecoense's new players faced Atletico Nacional in the South American Super Cup in 2017 [Getty Images]

In 2017, as Sudamericana champions, they once again had to face Atletico Nacional, the reigning Copa Libertadores winners, in the South American Super Cup.

It meant another flight to Medellin just months after the crash. This time Tozzo was on board.

"We went to see the exact location [of the crash]," he says. "I can't believe it was so close [to the airport]."

Chapecoense lost 6-3 on aggregate but later in the year won their state championship and finished as high as eighth in the national league in a demonstration of remarkable resilience.

The following year, in the second wave of new players, defender Bruno Pacheco was signed.

Pacheco, who has made nearly 150 appearances for the club in two spells, says: "Stepping on to the pitch at the arena was an emotional experience.

"I was representing those who are no longer with us, as well as the fans. I'm happy to be part of such an important chapter in the club's history."

After relegation from Serie A in 2019, Chapecoense won the Serie B title to earn promotion back to the top flight.

But that lasted just one season and they spent the next four terms in the second tier. They have spent this year in Serie A but will be relegated again.

Neto spoke at a ceremony in memory of the 71 passengers who died, marking the 10th anniversary of the tragedy [Getty Images]

After the crash, Neto's only appearance for Chapecoense came as a substitute in a charity friendly in December 2017, when money was raised to support relatives of the victims.

He remained at the club as a player for two more years until being forced to retire by the pain of his crash-related injuries.

He became a Christian evangelist, and he speaks for the relatives of his former team-mates who are still seeking justice as some families pursue compensation and hold out hope for criminal convictions.

Left-back Ruschel, who suffered severe injuries and had spinal surgery, was the only player to continue his professional playing career meaningfully, returning to the game nine months after the crash and staying with Chapecoense until 2021.

He only retired this November, helping his side Juventude win promotion to Serie A in his final game, ironically to swap places with Chapecoense.

Neto presented him with a commemorative plaque at half-time in Chapecoense's game against Palmeiras at the Arena Conda on 24 November when both men held aloft a jersey bearing Follmann's name.

Ruschel referenced the plane crash in a video announcing his retirement, calling it "a day that changed my life forever".

"I lost friends, companions and people with whom I shared dreams and projects," he said.

"And God gave me a second chance. I didn't know if I would be able to play football again, but I believed that if I was here, there was still a purpose for my life.

"And today, I have the privilege of being able to choose the moment to say goodbye."

Follmann's wedding - the one he had been preparing for before the crash - did happen and he became a father.

Despite having an offer to join Brazil's sitting volleyball team at the Paralympics, he turned to careers as a singer, motivational speaker and author, but with a new perspective.

"I observe everything around me. I observe life," he says.

"I have issues with making plans for the future, because life showed me that I only have today to live.

"I don't leave anything for tomorrow. I say everything today. I forgive today, I hug today."

Tozzo, the director who stayed at home, continues to live in Chapeco where he runs various businesses.

"I haven't talked about the accident for a long time," he says. "We keep remembering, and every time we talk, tears fall, but these are things in life that we have to face."

Additional reporting by Julia Dias Carneiro

#2648. Verso Torino-Lazio: tutte le novità sugli infortuni dei granata

Tra infortuni e il caso Rodriguez, il tecnico granata attende risposte dal campo prima della sfida contro la Lazio.

In vista della sfida tra Torino e Lazio, valida per la 13ª giornata di campionato, l'infermeria porta diversi dubbi in casa granata. Come riportato da Toro News, Abate deve valutare vari acciacchi emersi dopo Napoli e situazioni da chiarire tra difesa e fasce, pur con qualche buona notizia, e le ultime indicazioni sul campionato arriveranno direttamente dalle parole del tecnico prima del match.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Restano forti dubbi sull'impiego di Rafik Belghali contro la Lazio: il ginocchio destro infiammato (senza lesioni a menisco e legamenti) lo ha costretto al cambio al 40' al Maradona dopo aver stretto i denti al rientro anticipato dalla nazionale, e solo Abate chiarirà se potrà correre senza dolore. Stop più lungo per Ardian Ismajli: uscito nella ripresa a Napoli per una lesione di primo grado agli adduttori della coscia sinistra, salterà almeno tre settimane, a cui si somma l'operazione di osteosintesi alla mano destra per il quarto metacarpo che impone massima cautela.

Sulla sinistra resta in bilico Cristiano Biraghi, fermo a lavorare a parte per un affaticamento muscolare che lo staff valuterà giorno per giorno senza forzare, con convocazione incerta anche per la panchina. Segnali positivi invece da Niccolò Fortini, che ha superato la pubalgia ed è già tornato in panchina a Napoli: sta seguendo un percorso di potenziamento per ritrovare ritmo, e spetterà al tecnico decidere se impiegarlo con la Lazio o attendere ancora.

Il caso di Ricardo Rodriguez non è solo medico: dopo il recupero dall'infortunio pre Monza, ha risposto alla Svizzera giocando durante la sosta, attirando la dura reazione del Torino che lo ha escluso per motivi disciplinari a Napoli (scelta su cui Abate non ha avuto potere decisionale). Fisicamente sembra recuperato, ma resta da capire se verrà reintegrato per la sfida con i biancocelesti.

#2647. Kyle Shanahan: Brock Purdy's ankle sprain is "more mid than low"

49ers quarterback Brock Purdy emerged from Sunday’s win over the Vikings with an ankle injury. He’ll miss Sunday’s game against the Seahawks. Whether he’ll miss any games beyond that remains to be seen.

“It’s too soon, but I’m pretty optimistic about it,” coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Friday. “But, I was about this week to start and then it changes, so hopefully it’ll be all right.”

Next Sunday, the 49ers visit the Giants. The following weekend, the Rams visit.

Shanahan also revealed some details about the specific nature of the ankle sprain.

“Anytime it’s not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse,” Shanahan said. “Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. Didn’t heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down.”

Shanahan added that surgery isn’t on the table for Purdy.

Purdy’s performance in 2026 has made him one of the favorites to win the NFL MVP award.

#2646. Aaron Rodgers calls out Tom Brady for comments on locker room ‘sanctity’

Aaron Rodgers appeared to call out Tom Brady's "sanctity of an NFL locker room" comment in a text to Al Michaels that the Prime Video play-by-play broadcaster read during the Steelers' win over the Broncos on Friday.

"A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room, [Rodgers] said, 'The code of sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership,'" Michaels said, reading the message from Rodgers, which also included a claim that he was "barred" from the Pittsburgh facility.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) looks to pass against the Indianapolis Colts in Pittsburgh, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. Getty Images

Rodgers drew the criticism of Brady — and numerous analysts around the NFL — after his appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, during which he accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, breaking down a halftime huddle with "1-2-3 Packers" and missing walkthroughs. The comments followed the Steelers' decision to start Rudolph and make Rodgers inactive, which they announced Tuesday night.

And while Rodgers never referenced Brady by name in his message to Michaels, the "sanctity" line was the exact phrase that the former Patriots and Buccaneers star used.

Former NFL player Tom Brady looks on prior to a game between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers in Minneapolis, Sunday, Dec. 29, 2024. Getty Images

"The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place," Brady said Thursday on the Fox broadcast. "We shouldn't ever lose track of that as players. It's a privilege to be in that locker room. You're fighting with your teammates, you're fighting with your coaches, you're always acting as a team together. Shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public, that's what I'll say."

Brady overlapped with Rodgers in the NFL for most of his career before shifting into broadcasting after retirement, and it's unclear if Rodgers might need to contemplate a similar move after he was released by the Steelers on Wednesday.

The 42-year-old cleared waivers, but according to Prime Video reporter and NFL insider James Palmer on Thursday, teams have expressed little to no interest in signing Rodgers for the remainder of the season.

And for one night, the Steelers thrived without Rodgers, as a pair of defensive touchdowns and one touchdown pass from Rudolph improved their record to 7-4.

#2645. Heat 108, Knicks 105: “Really tough to win a poorly coached, corruptly reffed, half rotation injured game.”

The Knicks (12-7) lost two Emirates NBA Cup games this season but defeated the Cavaliers on Wednesday. Their chances of reaching the next round and continuing their defense of the Cup weren't nonexistent, but they needed to beat the Heat (11-7) by more than six points and for the Pacers to drop the Sixers.

First things first: the surging Heat are a handful even when New York's roster is complete. The Knicks had to meet the challenge without OG Anunoby (calf), Andre Drummond (concussion), Miles McBride (groin), and Jordan Clarkson (foot). The remaining players weren't altogether healthy, either: Karl-Anthony Towns (19 PTS, 10 RBS, 34 MIN) has an abdominal contusion, and Josh Hart (6 PTS, 9 RBS, 8 AST) is playing through a sore knee and shoulder. Our depleted Knickerbockers fell behind in the first quarter, then went down by 23 in the second. They cut their deficit to five in the third frame and had the Heat on the ropes in crunch time. A few missed free throws, an uncalled flagrant foul, and odd coaching decisions let the rally—and their Cup dreams—slip through their fingers. Final score: 108-105.

Quoth DWLLTheKnicksfan: "Really tough to win a poorly coached, corruptly reffed, half rotation injured game. Respect that it was close."

After the Knicks fell behind 15-7, coach Mike Brown replaced Hart with Pacôme Dadiet (4 PTS, 1 STL, 21 MIN, +7). Pac-Man played arm-flapping defense that disrupted the flow and led to a Miami turnover, then dunked a Brunson pass on the run. We're starting to see the vision! The French fella stayed on the floor when the next round of swaps came, playing alongside Brunson, Hart, Jose Alvarado (7 PTS, 15 MIN), and James Wiseman (11 PTS). The latter lasted just two minutes and committed a foul that heralded the return of Towns. Not a great first look on a night when Drummond was out.

New York logged nine boards in the first quarter. Giannis Antetokounmpo (22 PTS, 23 RBS, 32 MIN) matched that total alone, scarfing up most of Miami's 14 boards. A physical game had Towns wincing in pain, and we were wincing at New York's crappy shooting (2-of-11 from deep). With the Floridians sinking half of their three-pointers, the Knicks trailed 31-21 at the break.

In the second quarter, Mohamed Diawara and the Tylers (Kolek, Nickel) took the floor. Miami scored 12 unanswered while the 'Bockers continued to shoot like the Blind Boys of Alabama. The rookie Nickel looked lost and the coach bewildered. Mike Brown called for time when the score reached 48-27.

Out of that timeout, Brown sent Wiseman and Dadiet back in. Wiseman's minutes were rough. On consecutive plays, Wiggins picked off his inbound pass for a layup, and then Ryan Conwell intercepted his NEXT inbound pass. Unsurprisingly, he suffered a quick hook. Mike was running out of levers to pull as his team fell behind by 23. With four rotation players out and his starters all posting a plus-minus of -13 or worse, the coach fielded 11 different players in the first half in an attempt to slow Erik Spoelstra's squad, which scored inside, outside, and wherever else it wanted.

Thanks to a spirited late-half nine-oh run, the home team entered halftime trailing 60-44. There was plenty of blame to go around for our heroes. Towns (still painin'!) and Brunson combined for 25 of their team's 44 points, but the other starters had five points each, and the Knicks' bench had been outscored by its Miami counterpart, 30-4.

Through the half, the Flamingos shot 45% from the field and 36% from deep (9-of-25), while New York managed 40% and a miserable 21% (4-of-19). The Heat held only slight advantages in rebounds (24-23) and points in the paint (22-18) but were considerably better at protecting the ball. Nine Knicks turnovers yielded 11 Miami points, while the Heat committed just four turnovers that yielded three New York points. Worse, Miami won the battle for second-chance points, 10-0.

Over the first two minutes of the second half, Towns, Bridges, and Shamet combined for nine points to cut the deficit to 61-53. Miami fought back, but New York looked rejuvenated and alert (a marked improvement from the tryptophan blues of the first half). By the midway point of the quarter, the Knicks had converted five straight shots, reducing their deficit to five. As we've seen in game after game this season, it takes a lot of energy to climb out of deep holes. As the Knicks faltered, back-to-back Bridges turnovers allowed Giannis and Bam Adebayo (25 PTS, 7 RBS) to hammer Miami's lead back to 11.

Our heroes got an unexpected lift from Wiseman. He leaped into the fray, scoring seven points on three buckets and a free throw late in the third. That was more like it! Add a Brunson floater and an Antetokounmpo shot-clock violation, and New York trailed 86-79 at the horn.

Bam was a bother to start the fourth, netting two buckets, blocking shots by Shamet and Kolek, and drawing two fouls from Towns. Towns headed to the bench with four fouls at the 8:27 mark. Meanwhile, Shamet, Bridges, and Kolek each contributed layups to keep the Knicks within striking distance. The Heat struggled from the perimeter, with OAKAAKUYOAKs Tim Hardaway Jr. and Bobby Portis blowing opportunities to extend the lead.

Down 91-85 with plenty of game remaining, New York scored seven unanswered points, fueled by the bench mob. Wednesday's hero, Alvarado, scored five consecutive points, including a step-back three off his own offensive rebound, while Dadiet contributed a steal and a reverse layup off Brunson's eighth assist to give the Knicks their first lead. Davion Mitchell finally broke Miami's scoring drought with a floater, putting the Heat ahead 93-92 with six minutes remaining.

At the two-minute mark, the good guys trailed by three points after two freebies by Shamet. From there, Giannis launched an ill-advised, deep airball late in the shot clock; Brunson and Pelle Larsson traded free throws; Hart made one of two at the stripe; and Adebayo made the differential four with 44 seconds left. Captain Clutch's floater made it 104-102. Giannis missed two free throws with 14 seconds on the clock, and Adebayo fouled Wiseman on the loose ball, giving our heroes a soupçon of hope. My bingo card did not have Wiseman shooting free throws with the game on the line. How about yours?

The young journeyman made one, missed one, and Giannis snagged the board and called a timeout. 104-103, 13 seconds to go. When play resumed, Dadiet fouled Mitchell, who made both attempts. On the Knicks' inbounds play, the ball swung to Brunson in the corner, where he was fouled by Conwell. Even though Conwell violated JB's landing space, Scott "The Enforcer" Foster deemed it a common foul. Cap made two of three at the line. Spoelstra called a timeout. 106-105, nine seconds.

Larsson got a breakaway dunk—on the exact same inbounds play the Heat had run on their previous possession. Mike Brown elected not to call a timeout, and Brunson missed a contested triple to end the game.

This is your recap, chaps. As for the Knicks, they'll sleep in their own beds for a few more days and host the Hawks on Sunday. Rest up, troops.

#2644. 'Felt this team needed direction' - Rohit Sharma opens up on why he returned as MI captain for IPL 2027

'Felt this team needed direction' - Rohit Sharma opens up on why he returned as MI captain for IPL 2027 originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Rohit Sharma said he took the Mumbai Indians' captaincy back because the team badly needed direction.

Rohit hesitated over Akash Ambani's offer but chose to rebuild the team he led.

He admitted MI failed in three seasons and urged fans to support them.

MORE: Jasprit Bumrah overlooked for MI captaincy, reportedly rejects Rohit Sharma's deputy role: Is his future with MI in doubt?

Rohit Sharma has agreed to take charge of the Mumbai Indians again, and the answer is rooted in a belief that the side had lost its way. The batter, who led the franchise to five IPL titles, said he did not claim to be the only solution, but he felt the squad needed a clear sense of purpose and was ready to provide it.

The captaincy decision followed a miserable IPL 2026 for the five-time champions, who finished ninth on the table after winning only four of their 14 league games under Hardik Pandya. Rohit revealed that the slump was a regular topic of discussion at his house, where he spoke to his wife Ritika Sajdeh before MI co-owner Akash Ambani got in touch with him.

Sapru opened the discussion by pointing out the long bond Rohit shares with the dressing room and the management, and he asked how everyone had arrived at such a big decision.

"Look, I mean, as soon as we finished the IPL, we had a very disappointing season. And I was like, not just me, but many other players were quite frustrated with how we were playing," he said.

"Obviously, that's a natural thing for any athlete: if you are not playing well, if your team is not doing well, you know, you feel frustrated. And that is something that everyone was going through, and it was a tough period for everyone."

MORE: R Ashwin warns Rohit's MI captaincy return won't solve all problems

Rohit then moved from the general mood to his own reflections once he got back home. He accepted that a team that has tasted so much success can eventually go through a bad phase, and he placed the club's troubles in the wider context of sporting history.

"I went home, I thought about it that, man, it's not the team that used to be once upon a time," he said.

"We need to get back to that. What, how can we do that? It happens, it happens to any team: when you have seen such a high, there is bound to be a low. There is no doubt that all the great teams in our sporting history have gone through some kind of disappointment in their journey, and this was probably MI's journey of seeing disappointment."

MORE: 'Rohit is also a great captain': CSK CEO on MS Dhoni's relationship with MI

The conversation at home eventually led to a meeting with the franchise's leadership. Rohit said he began by discussing the situation with his wife, and the talks later widened after Akash Ambani rang him to explore the way ahead.

Rohit added: "So somewhere, going back home, we were thinking about it; I was talking to my wife about it, we were discussing and stuff. And then obviously Akash rang me up, we met, we discussed how to take this team forward, what can be done, and all of that. A lot of ideas came across, and yeah, he asked me whether I would be open to taking this team forward and all of that."

The batter was frank that his first reaction to the offer was not an enthusiastic yes. A lot had happened since he was replaced as captain ahead of IPL 2024, and he was unsure whether his state of mind allowed him to take up the role again.

"I mean, my honest thought initially was, 'I am not prepared for this right now; I have to go back and think about it,' because quite a lot had happened, so I didn't know if I was in that frame of mind to do it or not," he revealed.

"But then a feeling came from inside that, man, I am not saying that this team needs me as a leader, but this team needs a direction right now. And whatever that direction is, if it is me, I am more than happy to drive this team forward."

MORE: Fans go wild as Rohit Sharma returns as MI captain

Having made up his mind to think the matter through, Rohit weighed up what he could and could not do as captain. The turning point was a reminder of how much of the franchise he had shaped between 2013 and 2023, a period in which MI won five titles under him.

He said: "I went home, thought a little, understood a little about what it is, what I can do, what I cannot do, whether I can captain this team again or not, and all of that."

"But then, after thinking about so many things, I realized that, man, you know, this is the team that you built, you know, for 10 years you captained this team. I mean, I think it's time you try and accept that challenge again."

Mumbai Indians have ended up near the foot of the table in three of the last five seasons, finishing 10th in 2022 under Rohit himself, 10th in 2024 under Hardik and ninth in 2026.

"To see that MI was languishing at the bottom of the table for three seasons: one was during my tenure as well in 2022, then in 2024, and then 2026, that's not MI. That is not what MI is known for."

He went on to say that every team is trying hard to win and that Mumbai had simply not matched that level of competitiveness. The thought clearly troubled him on a personal level, because he still considers the franchise his own.

"It can happen; I mean, every other team in the competition is also trying to compete, but you have to compete harder, which we were not doing for all these years when we were languishing at the bottom," he analysed.

"We didn't compete properly; that's why we were failing to, you know, achieve as a team. I just felt that we fell short in a lot of ways—with our cricketing skills, with how we were approaching the game, and all that. So that is where we got stuck in all these years. It is disappointing to see that because, of course, it's, you know, at the end of the day, I am part of the team, and it's my team, and I can't see this team being like this."

Hardik was traded to Punjab Kings earlier this month in exchange for Arshdeep Singh. Rohit's return also comes with a revamped support staff, with Kieron Pollard now in charge as head coach.

Towards the end of the chat, Sapru asked Rohit if he had anything to say to the franchise's loyal supporters, who are known as the Paltan. His reply was a heartfelt plea for backing at a moment when results have not gone the team's way.

"Support us, man. I mean, it's just, this is the time we need you all the most. This is the time when everything is not working for us; we need you the most."

He added that he was not offering any promises in return: "I am not going to sit here and say, 'If you support us, we will do this or we will do that.' All I am trying to say is, we need you. And it is coming from the heart, because whatever they have done by coming out over all these years, they have had a huge hand in all the success we've had over the years. So I want them to play that hand again; to play that role of being our 13th man."

What stands out in this interview is Rohit's willingness to name the problem without hiding behind excuses. He did not blame one player or one season, and he said that the entire side had failed, himself included, since 2022 was among the years he mentioned as poor. That kind of honesty is a good starting point for any rebuild.

The challenge ahead is considerable, though. The squad has changed, Pollard is now running the coaching department, and the franchise will be measured against its own glorious past from the very first match of IPL 2027. Words alone won't repair a side that finished ninth.

#2643. Mike McCarthy admits he hasn't spent enough time with the defense

After registering an unlikely 27-5 win over the previously 8-2 Broncos, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn’t angry, resentful, or defiant.

He was the same guy he always is, and he admitted that (as former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said this week), McCarthy hasn’t been sufficiently invested in the side of the ball that isn’t his personal expertise.

“I have not spent enough time with the defense,” McCarthy told reporters. “You know, and that’s something that, as far as job responsibility, job description, you know, these are things that’ll be looked at in the offseason. But, you know, it’s a point in our year where we’re making adjustments and definitely conscientious of it. But at the end of the day, we have to all do our jobs and make sure we’re giving the players the plan and all the other things that they need that we can perform and play with that type of urgency, physicality that we played today.”

McCarthy prefaced his comments with a lesson he learned as a boy, growing up in Pittsburgh.

“My father used to tell me all the time as a kid, ‘You tell the truth, you only have to tell your story once,’” McCarthy said.

The truth is that this week has entailed two sharply different versions of reality, where both things can indeed be the truth. One, McCarthy (like all of us) has flaws. Two, Rodgers should not have spoken about them publicly.

Rodgers clumsily defended his decision to break the code of a football locker room by texting this to Al Michaels: “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.”

That’s fine, but how does disregarding the “sanctity” of the locker room (a word Rodgers undoubtedly selected in response to Tom Brady using it on Thursday) create “accountability”? McCarthy is accountable to team owner Art Rooney II. Not to the media or the fans.

And to what end? He was either doing it to help the Steelers save their season, or he was lashing out.

We’ll let you decide which explanation is more likely.

#2641. Rapid Recap: Pistons 113, Bucks 98

The Milwaukee Bucks started extremely well, but the Detroit Pistons' defence—which sits atop the league without Cade Cunningham—proved too much to overcome, and the Bucks lost 113-98. Brayden Burries led the Bucks with 23 points and seven rebounds, while Isaiah Joe starred for the Pistons with 22 points amid a spread of contributors.

The Bucks got off to a ripping start on both ends, taking advantage of the weapons the Pistons had out, running on misses to build a 10-2 lead and forcing an early timeout. Clearly, the timeout didn't do much, as Milwaukee stuck to their game plan, forcing Detroit into tougher shots and playing even more in transition as Kyle Kuzma, Jaime Jaquez Jr., and Ryan Rollins starred early for a combined 17 points—Bucks up 19-3 six minutes in! The Pistons finally got into gear after that as their bench filtered in, going on an 11-3 run as Tyler Herro and Myles Turner lost their men on the perimeter. Milwaukee would right the ship, though, as Brayden Burries checked in and scored a quick seven points to put the Bucks up 27-14 with two minutes to play. Unfortunately, some late mistakes by Milwaukee's youth allowed the Pistons to close on a 10-2 run, with the Bucks up 29-24 after one.

The Bucks started the second quarter with the same brand of silly basketball they finished the first with, repeatedly turning it over and taking bad shots as they went scoreless for nearly five minutes and let the Pistons take the lead. If not for Detroit missing a bunch of open shots, Milwaukee would have been in some strife. Luckily for the visitors, the game became a slog, and they stayed close, with neither team surpassing the 40-point mark until there was about three minutes to go. Yeah, it was ugly. Tyler Herro finally made his first field goal shortly thereafter, giving the Bucks a two-point edge, which they took into the locker room, up 50-48 at the half.

The Pistons came out ready and raring to go in the third, starting with an 11-4 run as Ausar Thompson began to make his mark. Both teams finally began to flow on offence as the Pistons nursed a 5-8-point advantage over the next few minutes, but a Bucks push cut the deficit to two, 71-69, with four to play. Milwaukee played decent half-court defence, but the minute they turned it over in live play—which they did a lot—Detroit almost always converted. That was, of course, until the final few minutes of the third, when the Pistons went bonkers no matter how they got their shots up, dominating on both ends as they closed on a 19-7 run—which included a buzzer-beating transition heave from Daniss Jenkins—to lead 90-76 after three.

Detroit kept turning up the defensive intensity early in the fourth, and with Tyler Herro resting, Milwaukee had nobody to calm them down and generate half-decent shots. Then we got some fireworks: Ausar Thompson beat Myles Turner down low—which he had done all night—shoved him in the chest, and the two came to blows, earning double technical fouls after Turner threw the ball at Thompson. From there, Detroit skied downhill as the Bucks struggled even to get shots up, and the deficit expanded to 20 points by the four-minute mark. It was all academic from that point forward as the wounded Pistons rolled over the Bucks.

I mean, to me it's just the Bucks' shooting percentage of 43.2%. What Detroit can do defensively, no matter who is sitting, is truly special.

The Bucks may never shoot well from three again.

Two nights after having won in Milwaukee, the Nets let Toronto hit first and they never hit back. Against an injured, offensively challenged team, they couldn't buy a bucket or beg a rebound in a sorry effort.

"I'm very sad about this disappointment, like everyone else," head coach Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez told reporters. "But this goes on. We have to lift our heads up."

Despite scoring a league-best 80 regular-season goals—led by Messi's 26 goals and 17 assists—Miami were shut out twice in a row. Stars including Luis Suarez, Rodrigo De Paul, Casemiro, and German Berterame could not find a breakthrough, with Casemiro seeing a goal disallowed and Berterame missing from point-blank range.

"But I'll say it again: the word 'failure' is very different when you don't try. This wasn't about names but rather performance. Gonzalez took charge just two months ago, kicking off his spell by guiding Inter Miami to the Campeones Cup title in September—the club's fourth trophy since Messi arrived in 2023. While Messi remains poised to clinch a historic third straight Landon Donovan MLS MVP award, the Argentine coach insisted an early exit does not define his squad's effort.

"I've been in charge for two months, and for me, the word 'failure' is too strong in life. This is soccer," Gonzalez added. "… And that's what soccer has: sometimes it's your turn, sometimes not. Now, it's our turn to be left out."

While interim head coach Laurent Courtois and the surging Crew advance to face either the New England Revolution or Philadelphia Union in the Eastern Conference Semifinals next weekend, Inter Miami enter an unexpectedly early offseason.

#2637. Steelers WR DK Metcalf clarifies he wasn't shouting out Aaron Rodgers via sign language after scoring TD

In case you somehow haven't heard, Aaron Rodgers was not playing for the Pittsburgh Steelers during their game on Black Friday. That doesn't mean he didn't come up.

Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf, one of Rodgers' closest teammates during his time in Pittsburgh, appeared to shout out the quarterback after scoring a touchdown in the first quarter against the Denver Broncos. The popular translation via American Sign Language: "Stand on business, eight." Eight was Rodgers' jersey number with the Steelers.

DJ Metcalf caught a touchdown pass from one quarterback then sent a message to another.

The trouble reportedly began when Rodgers made some sort of "ultimatum," as Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy put it, on Tuesday, which the team did not heed. Instead, Pittsburgh opted to bench Rodgers and start Rudolph against Denver, which led to Rodgers appearing on his friend Pat McAfee's show on ESPN on Wednesday and unleashing a torrent of grievances against McCarthy. The Steelers released Rodgers not long after.

Even more details were provided during the game Friday, as broadcaster Al Michaels shared the contents of a text from Rodgers, who claimed McCarthy ghosted him until the benching was announced and that the Steelers barred him from the facilities on Wednesday.

He made both free throws, and it gave the Hawks a four-point lead. The Celtics didn't call a timeout from there, ultimately accepting defeat, and the Hawks advanced to the knockout stage of the NBA Cup.

#2635. 5 quick hitters with Silver and Black Pride: Browns’ offense can take advantage of Raiders’ interior

This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns return from their bye at home as they take on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 12. To help preview a few topics from the Raiders' perspective, we reached out to Matt Holder from Silver and Black Pride and exchanged five questions with him.

Chris: "The Raiders are a big draw to watch again (at least to me) with Fernando Mendoza now starting. How have things looked for the first overall pick through two games?"

Matt: "Mendoza has certainly had his ups and downs over the last two weeks, as facing off against the Seahawks' and Broncos' defenses are brutal opponents to get your feet wet as a starting quarterback in the NFL. He had some issues deciphering Mike Macdonald's complex pressure looks and has taken way too many sacks (11) over the last couple of weeks. However, I thought he did a better job of feeling pressure and navigating the pocket in Denver. The Broncos were just able to get to him later in the game when the Raiders were trailing, and Denver's pass-rushers could pin their ears back.

Dawgs By Nature is SB Nation's home for Browns news, analysis, and conversation. Download the app to connect with fellow Cleveland diehards and share your take.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

One thing that Mendoza has brought to the offense is the ability to create off-script plays, which is ironic because that was viewed as one of his weaknesses coming out of Indiana. Don't get me wrong, Kirk Cousins did a great job operating the offense, but the 38-year-old's limited mobility and arm strength made it difficult for the offense to get out of bad situations. Meanwhile, the rookie has used his legs as a weapon, either by taking off and running or scrambling and making some impressive throws on the run. The clip below (link) highlights a few plays/throws that simply weren't happening with Cousins at quarterback.

So, there have definitely been some rookie struggles over the last two weeks. But the traits that made the No. 1 pick the No. 1 pick have shown up, and everyone in Raider Nation should be really excited about the future despite Mendoza being 0-2 as a starter so far."

Chris: "What do you view as the Raiders' biggest weakness on defense right now?"

Matt: "The defensive tackle position, and it's not particularly close.

Everyone knew Las Vegas' interior defensive line needed to be addressed in the offseason, but general manager John Spytek didn't add a defensive tackle until the seventh round of the draft. Now, according to Pro Football Focus, the Raiders' defensive tackle who has the highest pass-rush win rate (Thomas Booker IV at 8.6 percent) ranks 54th at the position among players with at least 74 pass-rush snaps.

Additionally, the two best run defenders at the position — Foley Fatukasi and Tim Keenan III — weren't even on the roster to begin training camp. Fatukasi had been available as a free agent for about six months before getting signed after the Raiders' first preseason game, while Keenan was a seventh-round pick by the Rams before failing to make Los Angeles' roster and getting added to Las Vegas' practice squad. To clarify, Keenan has played in the last five games and was added to the active roster a couple of weeks ago. As a result, the Raiders are allowing the second-most rushing yards per game (149.5) and are third-to-last in yards per carry allowed (4.8).

Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard is trying to run a variation of Macdonald's defense in Seattle, but Leonard simply doesn't have the talent on the interior of the defensive line that the Seahawks have to properly execute it. In my opinion, that's the biggest root cause of the defensive issues in Vegas."

Chris: "Cleveland went into Las Vegas last year around this same time and terrorized Geno Smith with ten sacks, and pretty much dominated that game. Besides QB, what are the biggest differences you see between last year's team and this year's that could make for a different outcome?"

Matt: "Klint Kubiak is the biggest difference. Last year's Browns game ended up being Chip Kelly's last as offensive coordinator, with Pete Carroll firing Kelly shortly after the contest. The rumor is that Carroll was forcing Kelly to run a specific type of offense instead of letting the play caller put together his own scheme, and I can say that Kelly's offense looked nothing like I expected it to be with very generic play calling and little to no creativity.

Meanwhile, Kubiak is in full control as the head coach and offensive play-caller. Whether it's Cousins or Mendoza at quarterback, the Raiders' offensive scheme has been much better than it was a year ago. That's led to a dramatic difference in points per game, going from ranking dead last at 14.2 ppg to 11th at 25.0 ppg. Fun fact: It only took 10 games for the 2026 team to surpass the 2025 team's point total (241) for the entire season.

Also, while the Raiders' current offensive line is far from perfect, the unit is better than last year's at this point in the season. Of the six linemen who played against the Browns last year, only one remains on the current active roster: right tackle DJ Glaze, who is arguably the team's most improved player. So, while I mentioned previously that sacks were an issue for Mendoza, he's already shown growth in that area, and the line is better than it was at this point a year ago."

Chris: "Tell us about one player who Browns fans may not have heard of, but who could have an impact on this Sunday's game."

Matt: "I'm going to cheat and go with two, one on each side of the ball: wide receiver Jack Bech and safety Treydan Stukes.

Bech, the 2025 second-round pick, is coming off his best game as a pro with eight catches for 88 yards and a touchdown. Week 10 was ugly, where he had a couple of drops and was unproductive with just two grabs and 10 yards. However, Bech and Mendoza seem to have good chemistry together, as the second-year wideout leads the team with 15 targets over the last two weeks, per PFF. He isn't a great athlete who is going to generate a ton of separation on his routes, but the TCU product is good on contested targets and at finding holes in zone coverage.

Stukes, the 2026 second-round pick, has primarily been a free safety and has done well in that role. He's constantly around the ball, with a pair of interceptions, five passes defended and several quality tackles to limit gains in both the passing and running games. Recently, the coaching staff has been tapping into the Arizona product's versatility, playing him at some nickelback (his college position) and having him line up against tight ends. It wouldn't surprise me if we see Stukes and Harold Fannin Jr. face off against each other frequently on Sunday."

Chris: "The Browns are underdogs against the Raiders on Sunday (Browns -4.5 as of this question, per FanDuel). Who would you pick to win the game?"

Matt: "Call me a homer, but I kind of like the Raiders to pull off the upset. Cleveland has become known for having slow starts and making fourth-quarter comebacks so far this season, ranking 31st in first-quarter points per game (1.3) but tied for 10th in fourth-quarter ppg (7.4). Meanwhile, Las Vegas' defense has generated the most fourth-quarter turnovers (10, h/t Ari Meirov on X/Twitter), three more than any other team, and ranks 10th in ppg allowed (6.1) during the final frame.

So, I think that tilts in the Silver and Black's favor, and the numbers above remind me of the Saints game from earlier in the season, where the Raiders won as underdogs in New Orleans. I'll go 24-21 Vegas."

Thanks again to Matt for taking the time to answer my questions.

#2633. Nets blow another opportunity, collapse in 124-100 loss to Raptors

It's hard getting a grasp on who the Nets are these days.

Some nights, they look like they're making progress even if it doesn't equal a victory. Building momentum is the issue. After taking down the two-win Bucks on Wednesday, the matchup marked the start of a lighter patch of Brooklyn's schedule, playing a 6-11 Raptors team without Kawhi Leonard and RJ Barrett.

These are the games the Nets need to get. Instead, it's players like Immanuel Quickley — who dropped 21 points in the third quarter en route to a 24-point triple double — that ultimately doom teams like the Nets. Or they just do it to themselves.

They struggled to build a potential win streak and fell 124-100 at the hands of the Raptors, outscored 39-24 in the third quarter.

Right out of the gate, both teams applied heavy ball pressure. Toronto has a reputation for doing just that and the Nets turned the ball over four times, compared to the Raptors' two.

There were a ton of lead changes, but by the end of the frame, the Raptors were ahead by four. The Nets' offensive engine was simple from early on: Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. In the first quarter, they combined for 17 of Brooklyn's 27 points, with Porter Jr. posting nine points in nine minutes while Randle finished the quarter with eight points in 10 minutes.

Jordi Fernández went to the bench earlier than normal, with nine players logging minutes in the first quarter. It feels as if he has changed his philosophy recently, feeding more into the rhythm of the game and making changes based on that rather than a predetermined notion of how minutes are distributed.

Entering the game, the Raptors had established a reputation for doing the tiny things right, like applying ball pressure and winning the rebounding battle, but they just couldn't shoot well enough to finish close games.

However, the tone of the game shifted completely by halftime. It turned into an offensive shootout, even as Brooklyn still trailed 63-55. Randle and MPJ remained the Nets' top offensive threats, combining for 27 of Brooklyn's 55 first-half points.

At the half, both teams were shooting over 50% from the field, while the Nets shot a whopping 42.1% from 3-point range. Toronto's mark from downtown wasn't too shabby either, at 38.9%. The Nets struggled to take advantage of the freebies, though, shooting just 58.3% from the charity stripe, leaving five points on the table in an eight-point game by the break.

Brooklyn's toughest task in the first half was containing Scottie Barnes, who dropped 22 points in 17 minutes on 7-of-12 shooting, including a 2-of-4 mark from downtown. He led Toronto's offense early before finishing the night with 34 points.

It was a close game throughout the first half. Coming out of the break, though, that narrative flipped in an instant. Call it the Nets continuing to fulfill that "two-face" identity. You don't even have to look at it game by game to get that takeaway; it's quarter by quarter, as it was on Friday.

After the third quarter, Toronto led 102-79. All it took was one quarter, in which the Nets lost 39-24, to really put themselves in a tough hole after a pretty solid first half. On top of Barnes, Immanuel Quickley emerged as another offensive problem for the Nets, scoring 21 points in the third quarter, leading the Raptors' 39-point frame.

The damage was already done. Toronto maintained its 23-point advantage for most of the fourth quarter before closing out the 124-100 victory.

If you're looking for positives as a Nets fan, Mikel Brown Jr. set a career high with 21 points in 25 minutes and arguably put out his best game as a pro yet. Other than that, the lack of defense continues to crush Brooklyn, especially playing a team like Toronto that possesses offensive firepower.

Because of that, the Nets are now 4-14 on the season after Friday's loss.

Final score: Toronto Raptors 124, Brooklyn Nets 100

The Nets will evaluate Brown Jr. to see whether he'll play in his first full back-to-back.

The rookie had a career-high 21 points in 25 minutes.

It's a quick turnaround for the Nets, who head to Charlotte to play the second leg of their back-to-back tomorrow. After the Hornets tomorrow, they'll face Thunder two times in a row, Celtics, Pistons, Mavericks, Magic, Wizards, Blazers, and Spurs.

#2632. 2026 Week 13 Preview: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs @ Georgia Southern Eagles

Time and date: Saturday, November 28 at 12:00 p.m. ET

Location: Paulson Stadium — Statesboro, GA

All-time series: Georgia Southern leads, 1-0

Last meeting: Georiga Southern 38, Louisiana Tech 3 — December 23, 2020 (New Orleans Bowl)

Current streak: Georgia Southern, 1 (2020)

It's the Sun Belt game of the year. An interdivision matchup perfectly set up for the final week of the regular season, with massive implications for both sides. The winner secures hosting duties for the 2026 Sun Belt Championship Game, an event neither team has ever participated in before.

If Louisiana Tech wins, the Bulldogs finish their inaugural Sun Belt season at 8-0, and they will host the Sun Belt Championship Game in Ruston. However, they may not receive a rematch with Georgia Southern. An Eagles loss combined with a James Madison victory over Coastal Carolina sends the Dukes to their second consecutive Sun Belt title game.

Thus, it is especially imperative for Georgia Southern to win. If the Eagles prevail over the Bulldogs, they will set the scene for a rematch in Statesboro, GA exactly six days later.

Both teams are scorching hot. Louisiana Tech has won eight consecutive matchups, while Georgia rides a five-game win streak, and most of the wins on those streaks were definitive double-digit victories. But when two streaking teams collide, one of those streaks must end.

Louisiana Tech (9-2, 7-0 Sun Belt) is tied for the third-longest win streak in the country, entering Saturday's pivotal matchup having won eight consecutive games.

The Bulldogs remain perfect in conference play since joining the Sun Belt, and they've won their league games by an average margin of 23.9 points per game. Other than the 1-point comeback win over Louisiana, Sonny Cumbie's team has defeated each conference foe by at least 15 points, getting better on both sides of the ball as the season progresses.

Blake Baker has hit his stride offensively, and the junior is one of the most efficient quarterbacks in the country. His 72.6 completion percentage ranks second nationally, and his 21-to-1 touchdown to interception ratio is tied with Wake Forest's Gio Lopez as the best among all quarterbacks with at least 20 touchdown passes.

The Bulldogs' offense thrives mainly through the air. The run game ranks 86th in the FBS, but the passing game checks in at 25th in yards per game. Baker's primary targets are wide receiver Jalen Mickens, whose 61 receptions and 809 yards lead the team, and tight end Eli Finley. Finley is one of three finalists for the John Mackey Award, and he owns the most receiving yards among all FBS tight ends.

Louisiana Tech's defense has held three of its seven Sun Belt opponents completely out of the end zone. The Bulldogs are elite backfield invaders, producing the third-most tackles for loss and the 12th-most sacks per game in the country. Outside linebacker Alonzo Jackson Jr. has been at the forefront of the dominance, and the Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year candidate has more sacks (11.0) and tackles for loss (18.5) than anyone else in the conference.

The Bulldogs don't just produce pressure. They also produce opportunities. Their defense ranks second nationally with 28 takeaways and second nationally with a +17 turnover margin. Cornerback Jordan McRae is at the centerpiece of all the havoc, taking four interceptions back for a nation's best 195 yards and two touchdowns. Thanks to all the pressure and takeaways, only one opponent has eclipsed 20 points on the Louisiana Tech defense in the past six games.

Georgia Southern (7-4, 6-1 Sun Belt) showed flashes of brilliance during a 1-3 non-conference showing. Those flashes have come to fruition in the form of wins, and now the Eagles are on the verge of their first-ever Sun Belt Championship Game appearance.

It's win-and-in for Tyson Helton's team, which has won five consecutive games by an average margin of 23.0 points per game. Georgia Southern's lone defeat came against James Madison in mid-October, falling inches short on a missed field goal away from forcing overtime.

Since that lone conference slip-up, Georgia Southern has become a force offensively. The Eagles have scored 128 points across their last three matchups, and seventh-year senior Max Johnson is unleashing the best version of himself. The well-traveled quarterback has maintained his efficiency while keeping the offense vertical. He completes 69.9 percent of passes, delivering 20 touchdowns against three interceptions.

Johnson works with one of the deeper receiving corps in the country, one featuring five different targets with at least 340 receiving yards. Topping the list is Alex Taylor, whose 691 yards and five touchdowns lead the Eagles. Josh Dallas is also a pivotal possession receiver, securing a team-high 56 receptions and regularly converting in short yardage situations. Jeremiah Ware, Andre Greene Jr., and tight end River Helms are among other frequented options in the nation's 18th-ranked passing offense.

The Eagles don't run often, attempting the 12th-fewest runs per game. However, they remain efficient with over 4.3 yards per carry behind a stout offensive line that rarely allows sacks.

The reason for Georgia Southern's vast improvement can be seen on the defensive side. First-year coordinator Mike Mutz has turned the unit into No. 19 in scoring defense and No. 21 in scoring defense. The Eagles haven't surrendered more than 27 points in conference play and have held five straight opponents to 15 points or fewer.

Georgia Southern is tied for 24th nationally with 30 sacks, and it's been a concerted effort across the entire unit, and defensive end Anthony Bynum ranks atop the team with 5.0. The pressure created at the line of scrimmage helps the Eagles' defensive versatility, and they are in the top 25 of the FBS in both pass defense and run defense.

Two streaking offenses meet two relentless defenses, and something has to give on both sides as two of the hottest teams in America meet in Statesboro. Georgia Southern enters with homefield advantage in what could be the program's greatest crowd since joining the FBS, given the unforeseen stakes of Saturday's contest.

Both teams enjoy similar strengths — the passing attack, limiting interceptions, and creating pressure on defense. This one has the makings of a close game, but Louisiana Tech has been the more battle-tested team, showing poise in a dramatic comeback against Louisiana and a narrow win over Army. In a close game, that experience might matter, and the Bulldogs finish their inaugural Sun Belt season with a perfect 8-0 record.

Prediction: Louisiana Tech 28, Georgia Southern 27
