#2631. No. 3 Texas at Texas A&M final score: Longhorns defense holds late in 16-6 win

A berth in the SEC championship game and a first-round by in the College Football Playoff are on the line for the No. 3 Texas Longhorns in the Lone Star Showdown against the Texas A&M Aggies on Friday in College Station.

After Texas won the toss and deferred to the second half, Texas A&M picked up one first down before punting away to the Longhorns, who went three and out, but freshman wide receiver Kohen Brown recovered the muffed punt and senior kicker Gianni Spetic connected from 54 yards when the drive stalled.

Struggling to catch kicks, the Aggies had to start their second possession on their own 7-yard line because of another muff.

Overcoming a holding penalty on first down and a delay of game penalty on third down, Texas A&M quarterback Brady Hart completed a 10-yard pass against Texas senior cornerback Bo Mascoe to move the chains, doing so again on third down when Mascoe was flagged for pass interference. Into Longhorns territory, the Aggies had a decision to make on 4th and 3 from the 40-yard line, opting to take a delay of game and punt the ball away.

Good pass protection on 3rd and 3 allowed Texas senior quarterback Arch Manning to connect with sophomore tight end Emaree Winston for a 14-yard gain, then hit junior wide receiver Emmett Mosley V for 13 yards. Snapping the ball before the end of the first quarter, Manning improvised on a shovel pass to fifth-year running back Raleek Brown for eight yards on 2nd and 9.

In 21 personnel, sophomore running back Michael Terry III took a handoff, got vertical, and ran through a tackle attempt for an 18-yard gain. Looking to score for just outside the red zone, Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian called a double pass for junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo, who made a good decision not to throw it, instead settling for a two-yard gain.

Put behind the chains when a nine-yard reception by fifth-year tight end Michael Masunas was negated by offensive pass interference, the Longhorns got into a manageable 3rd and 3 thanks to an 18-yard reception by Wingo on an free-access throw by Manning. After a lengthy injury timeout for a Texas A&M defender, a designed quarterback run for Manning moved the chains with the help of some leg drive from the Texas quarterback.

In an empty formation, Manning connected with Masunas on a short pass that gained 13 yards.

On 1st and goal from the 3-yard line, Manning's pass was tipped at the line of scrimmage, but managed to flutter its way into the strong hands of junior wide receiver Cam Coleman, who had a two-way go and ran a good slant route to score the touchdown and go up 10-0.

With former starting quarterback Marcel Reed into the game, two carries by Reed went for four yards before his departure in favor of Hart. On 3rd and 6, an easy-access throw when senior linebacker Rasheem Biles got lost in coverage resulted in a first down.

Hart misfired on a slant on 2nd and 10, forcing a more difficult conversion. A comeback to Isaiah Horton went for eight yards, but A&M head coach Mike Elko made another conservative decision to punt on 4th and 2.

Terry flashed his athleticism with a hurdle on second down to pick up eight yards and a first down, carrying it two more times for three yards and eight yards. On a toss sweep to Terry, the play got blown up by a linebacker coming downhill for a six-yard loss. After a tunnel screen to Mosley, a deep over to the Stanford transfer was delivered well by Manning under pressure, but Mosley couldn't extend to make the grab, forcing a punt.

Trying to throw the ball on first down, Hart held it too long and Texas senior edge Brad Spence beat the running back in pass protection for a sack. After sophomore nickel back Graceson Littleton broke up a screen pass on second down, Hart had to throw the ball away on 3rd and 17.

A friendly roll on the 53-yard punt by Tyler White flipped the field. Scrambling for eight yards, Manning started the drive positively, and appeared to pick up a first down with a scramble on 3rd and 10 that was negated by a holding call against senior left tackle Melvin Siani.

After Texas punted, Texas A&M mounted an effective drive highlighted by a 19-yard reception by Aaron Gregory and a pass-interference penalty on senior safety Jelani McDonald on 3rd and 3 at the edge of field-goal range. David Olano ultimately finished the half with a 52-yard field goal to make it 10-3.

The Longhorns opened the second half with an incompletion targeting Coleman, who was held at the top of his route, and a short run by Brown to set up 3rd and 9. Forced to check down to Winston, the sophomore tight end was dropped near the line of scrimmage for a three and out.

Another easy-access completion to Mario Craver on a slant initially appeared to be a positive second-down play, but Craver just lost the football turning up the field and McDonald recovered. A lengthy review upheld the call on the field and Texas took over at A&M's 34-yard line.

With the Longhorns offensive line struggling to create any creases in the running game, Brown was dropped for no gain before freshman wide receiver Jermaine Bishop Jr. caught a short pass and gained six yards. Facing 3rd and 4, Coleman won over the middle for a first down.

Throwing a screen to Wingo from a bunch formation to the field, the blocking didn't hold up and Wingo was tackled for no gain. Looking for a touchdown, Sarkisian called a wheel route for Brown, who ran a good route against man coverage and won, but Manning couldn't deliver the ball on time because of pressure in his face and sailed it too far when he could try to make the throw. Needing to convert 3rd and 10, Manning connected with Terry for a catch spotted at nine yards. When Texas A&M called timeout before Texas went for it on 4th and 1, a sneak by Manning that created a lot of movement at the line of scrimmage.

Operating with a lack of urgency under center on 1st and 10 from the 11-yard line, Manning got a delay of game penalty, then missed Coleman on a glance run-pass option and Mosley on a back-shoulder fade. Unable to get a play called in a timely manner, Texas had to burn its first timeout of the second half to run a 3rd and 15 play, a double move to Coleman that never had a chance.

The Horns had to settle for a 33-yard field goal by Spetic and a 13-3 lead.

Looking for a big play on 2nd and 4, Gregory used a double move to beat Mascoe, who had to hold to negate the explosive play. A slot fade to Gregory on 3rd and 4 beat Littleton for a 30-yard gain, and A&M was on the edge of the red zone.

Two runs by Carsyn Baker netted zero yards and Hart came under quick pressure, forcing him to throw underneath to Gregory for six yards, resulting in a 35-yard field goal to make it 13-6.

A rare kickoff return for senior Ryan Niblett was returned for 32 yards to the 35-yard line, but Brown was cut down for a one-yard gain on first down. On 2nd and 9, a comeback route for Coleman resulted in a run after the catch and an important 19-yard gain.

The drive quickly lost momentum when Brown didn't run a route as Manning expected and the Texas quarterback nearly threw an interception trying to find Mosley over the middle. A pass to Coleman was completed just short of the first down and Sarkisian decided to go for it on 4th and 1, a handoff to Terry that was stuffed in the backfield.

After a four-yard completion on first down, McDonald came downhill with aggression against the run and inflicted a tackle for loss. On 3rd and 7, senior linebacker Justin Cryer wrapped his blitz around sophomore defensive end Lance Jackson and sacked Hart for a big loss that ended the third quarter.

After A&M's punt, Texas took over at its 38-yard line, where Manning scrambled for 13 yards by identifying man coverage and taking advantage of the space that afforded him. A personal foul for going low on a Longhorns offensive lineman resulted in 15 yards for Texas. On 2nd and 7 looking for a shot play, Manning took a five-yard sack with nowhere to throw the ball. A bubble screen to Wingo picked up 19 yards behind a good block from Mosley and an escort from the offensive line.

Mosley drew a holding penalty on a pass over the middle that would have otherwise gone for a touchdown, but another pass over the middle, this time to Wingo, went incomplete. On 2nd and goal, a designed run to the boundary for Manning was dropped for a loss. Trying to throw into a small window, Manning's pass was knocked into the air and intercepted in the end zone.

Beat in press man coverage, Mascoe gave up a 33-yard completion to Gregory before senior safety Derek Williams nearly came up with an interception on the next throw by Hart, also targeting Gregory. Going for it on 4th and 3, A&M called a timeout before spreading the field and targeting sophomore cornerback Kade Phillips, whose coverage on Horton forced a turnover on downs.

Brown found some running room on first down and the Aggies were called for a hands to the face penalty. Needing to break one open-field tackle for a big play, Brown was brought down instead, then tackled for a loss on second down. Facing 3rd and 7, Manning took the edge on a designed run, broke a tackle, and fell forward for a massive first down.

Looking for Wingo, the out route went for seven yards and kept the clock moving. A predictable run on 2nd and 3 was stopped for a three-yard loss and Manning had to throw the ball away on third down. Clutch as he has been all season, Spetic knocked the 42-yard field goal down the middle to make it a two-score game at 16-6 with 5:19 remaining.

In desperation mode, the Aggies went for a 4th and 1 deep in their own territory and converted it, then benefitted from a roughing the passer penalty on Jackson. Willing to trade short completions for time coming off the clock, the Texas defense forced A&M into another 4th and 1. Disorganized, the Aggies had to use their final timeout before Hart threw incomplete, setting the Horns up to ice the game.

Running hard up the middle, Terry broke a tackle for a first down, sending the game into the two-minute timeout and allowing the Horns to finish the game in victory formation to clinch a berth in the SEC championship game.

#2630. Celtics lose Group C to Hawks 87-86, will be Play-In wildcard

Jalen Johnson and the Hawks' defense proved too much for the Celtics in a 87-86 loss in the final game of NBA Cup group play. Boston had a chance to lock up East Group C and home-court advantage through the semifinals of the NBA Cup's elimination rounds, but the loss allowed the Hawks to win the group via tiebreaker.

However, their record and point differential still leave the team with the wild card spot, so the team is set to face the Detroit Pistons in the quarterfinals.

Boston started Derrick White, Hugo Gonzalez, Paul George, Jayson Tatum, and Neemias Queta against Atlanta. Mitchell Robinson remained out as he recovers from COVID for the fourth straight game.

The Hawks started Kingston Flemings, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson, and Onyeka Okongwu. The team's loaded injury report included CJ McCollum, Jock Landale, Mouhamed Gueye, Asa Newell, and Henri Veesaar.

The game got going with a couple ugly offensive possessions for the C's, but Gonzalez put Boston on the scoreboard with a putback layup off a Queta miss. Luckily, the Hawks also had a rough start and missed their first 5 shot attempts of the game. Daniels was the first to break the ice for Atlanta by hitting a three-pointer from the corner, but the early game was defined by defense.

While the Celtics struggled to break free from their defenders along the perimeter, Gonzalez hit the team's first three-pointer of the game off an assist from Tatum to put Boston up 8-3. That score held for a couple minutes, as neither team could score consistently. However, the Hawks had the hardest time breaking through, as they missed 11 of their first 12 shots from the field.

With about 6 minutes left in the quarter, the bench was subbed in to play alongside Tatum and made an immediate impact as Baylor Scheierman hit a three-pointer that was only possible due to an offensive rebound by Luka Garza, who got a layup of his own shortly after. At that point, both teams got into a better offensive rhythm. JT took a more active role on the floor and hit a couple shots, while Johnson and Luguentz Dort sunk a couple of their own. By the time Payton Pritchard finished a layup with 2:23 to go in the quarter, the Celtics were ahead 21-12.

The Hawks' perimeter defense was doing a great job at running the C's off of the line, so Boston attacked the paint early and often. That attack resulted in a solid contested layup by Tatum, who followed it up with a slick step-back three-pointer on the next trip down the court. He had 13 points in the first quarter alone.

The Celtics finished the quarter in dominant fashion, as Pritchard hit a three-pointer and the defense locked down the Hawks to end the frame.

Boston opened the second quarter with a 29-14 lead, but immediately surrendered a three-pointer and turned the ball over on their side of the court. Queta got the scoring going with an easy layup over Daniels. A couple plays later, Queta got an offensive rebound and passed it out to Sam Hauser for an open three-pointer.

That started off an impressive little stretch by Hauser, who then got an offensive rebound of his own off a missed Pritchard three-pointer and put it back for an easy layup, then stole the ball on a bad pass from Corey Kispert. However, he was subbed out soon after in favor of Ron Harper Jr.

The Hawks scored a quick 5 points to narrow Boston's lead to 37-25, and had a chance to cut it to 10, but White got a nice block on Okongwu and got it ahead to George for a transition layup and his first points of the game. Unfortunately for George, he racked up 4 turnovers over his first 12 minutes of play and was subbed out with a little more than 6 minutes to go in the frame.

BOSTON, MA – NOVEMBER 27: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics drives to the basket during the game against the Atlanta Hawks during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 27, 2026 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Tatum came back into the game around the same time and hit another contested layup to put the C's up 43-30 with less than 5 minutes to go in the half, but Boston looked a little sloppy and called a timeout about a minute later.

Following the break, Tatum missed a tough shot but got immediate redemption with a steal that led to a Gonzalez transition layup. Gonzalez also hit a beautiful floater while driving down the lane a couple plays later. While White masterfully broke up a fast break by the Hawks, Atlanta's offense clearly started clicking before halftime. They scored 9 points over the final 3 minutes of the half, which finished with the C's up 51-39.

At halftime, Tatum had 16 points — which led the team — on 54.5% shooting from the field, along with 4 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 steals.

No other Celtic finished the first half with double-digit points, but Gonzalez wasn't far behind with 9 points on 4-6 shooting. Queta had only 3 points, but was incredibly active on the boards, as he racked up 12 rebounds.

On the Hawks' side of things, Johnson led the way with 12 points (on 4-12 shooting), 7 rebounds, 2 assists, and 3 stocks. Like Tatum, he was the only player on his team to finish with double-digit points.

Overall, the half closed with the Celtics shooting 50% from the field and 40% from three-point range, while the Hawks shot 28.9% from the field and 19.2% on three-pointers. However, Atlanta put up 7 more field goal attempts than Boston and 11 more three-point attempts.

Coming out of the half, White got a nice steal, but George's off night continued as he missed an open three-pointer. The Hawks capitalized and started the second half with a much stronger offensive showing than the C's. They went on a 9-4 run to cut the lead to 7 points less than 2:30 into the third quarter, with Johnson scoring 7 of Atlanta's 9 points during the stretch.

That's when George finally woke up. He hit two three-pointers over the course of three offensive possessions to bring Boston's lead back up to 13 points but, unfortunately for the Celtics, everyone else went cold. Tatum missed an easy, wide-open corner three-pointer, and White missed another open 3 the next time down, leading Head Coach Joe Mazzulla to call a timeout the next time the C's got the ball.

It didn't help much, though. While Hauser was subbed in for White, the Celtics could not buy a shot from deep. On the other hand, the Hawks scored 10 of the first 12 points scored out of the break and cut the lead down to 5, 65-60, with less than 4 minutes to go in the third quarter — leading Boston to call another timeout.

When play resumed, Garza cut into the paint for a nice layup, but the C's surrendered a three-pointer to Johnson and another to Aaron Wiggins a few plays later. By the time Kispert cut in for an easy layup with 1:30 to go in the frame, the lead had been chipped down to 69-68.

Daniels gave the Hawks their first lead of the night with a floater with 12 seconds to go, and Tatum missed a layup to end the quarter. Atlanta finished the frame with a 70-69 lead.

The Celtics still looked disjointed as the fourth quarter began, but White got a steal and knocked down a layup to put Boston on top again — at least until Dort hit a couple free throws to retake the lead. Pritchard hit a good-looking floater, but it was negated by a shot clock violation. Thankfully, he hit a step-back three-pointer from the top of the arc soon after to tie the game up at 74 with about 10 minutes left in the game.

Nevertheless, the momentum remained in the Hawks' favor, as Dort hit a three-pointer and drew a charge on Garza, which was upheld after a ridiculously long official review. The failed challenge left the C's with 2 timeouts with 9 minutes left to go.

With the help of a Queta free throw and a Hauser three-pointer, the C's took a 78-77 lead with 7:48 remaining. Tatum was subbed back in soon after, but he struggled to get the offense going again. On one play, Boston got multiple offensive boards, but missed all three shot attempts of the possession. On top of that, the refs were stingy with the whistle and called offensive fouls on both Queta and George, ending 2 possessions prematurely.

Fortunately for the Celtics, the Hawks offense also came back down to earth, and a few minutes passed without any scoring on either side. The next points weren't scored until the 4:38 mark of the fourth quarter, when Okongwu hit a floater to put the Hawks up 79-78. The Hawks got the next bucket on a Johnson dunk and took a 3-point lead with 4:06 to go.

Turnovers were killer. Queta, who was dominant on the boards and set a new personal record of 21 rebounds with 3 minutes left in the game, turned the ball over twice in quick succession. Tatum then lost his handle and lost a ball out of bounds.

The Celtics didn't score again until Dort fouled White, who knocked down a pair of free throws to narrow the Hawks' lead to 83-81 with 1:42 left in the game. White then hit a floater on the next offensive possession to tie the game at 83 with 1:10 to go.

Alexander-Walker followed up White's buckets with a driving dunk to retake the lead for Atlanta, and Johnson blocked Tatum on a drive into paint to prevent the tying bucket. With 11.9 seconds remaining and the Hawks with the ball, Tatum got a steal but turned the ball over again right after. Alexander-Walker sealed the game with a pair of free throws that put Atlanta up 87-83 with 3 seconds left to go. White hit a buzzer-beating three-pointer in the remaining time, but it wasn't enough to get the win

Tatum finished the game with 20 points on 36.4% shooting from the field, 9 rebounds, 5 assists, and 4 steals.

Queta racked up 11 points, 22 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 stocks.

On the Hawks' side, Johnson finished with 24 points and 12 rebounds, while Alexander-Walker finished with 20 points and a couple crucial last-minute plays.

The Celtics will play Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs next at 4 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 29, at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio.

#2629. Buffalo Gap football secures spot in state playoffs

SWOOPE — Buffalo Gap is headed back to the state playoffs for a second straight year. The Bison beat Altavista 28-16 Nov. 27 to win the Region 1B championship and earn a spot in the Class 1 state playoffs.

Senior Cooper Reed scored three touchdowns and Zane Emurian added another score while the defense held a potent Altavista team which was averaging 39 points a game to less than half that total.

It was the third year in a row the two teams met in the playoffs. Gap now owns two wins in those three meetings.

Buffalo Gap will host a state semifinal game Saturday, Dec. 5. A win in that game would send the Bison to Salem for the Class 1 state championship.

Buffalo Gap took the early lead on a Reed touchdown before Altavista tied the game on a Cortez Moon touchdown run. Emurian put the Bison back in front 14-7, but in the final seconds of the half Altavista kicked a field goal to get within four points at the break.

The biggest play of the game may have been on defense in the third quarter. Altavista got the ball near midfield to start the second half after recovering an onside kick by the Bison. But on second-and-7 from the 35, Ace Long's hard hit forced a fumble and Gap's Bradley Shiplett came up with the recovery.

Buffalo Gap got the ball at its own 35 with 8:38 showing on the clock. The Bison went on a 15-play drive that ate up all but the final 37 seconds of the third quarter. Gap converted two third downs and a fourth down on the drive before Reed scored to put the Bison in front 21-10.

"That was huge," Reed said of the defensive play and the offensive drive. "Ace Long, our hype guy, forced the fumble. Big hit on the running back. And then we came down and burned a ton of clock."

Another Reed touchdown put the game mostly out of reach as the Bison held on for the victory.

Buffalo Gap coach Brad Wygant said it was clear in the offseason that the veterans were motivated by the way last season ended. The Bison lost on the road in the state semifinals 38-32 to Rappahannock. Gap had the ball on the 7 with less than a minute left, but couldn't get in the end zone as they watched their season come to an end.

Rappahannock went on to win the state championship the following week. Wygant said his players realized that could have just as easily been them celebrating a state title. He believes that motivated them to work even harder in the offseason.

Reed said they will take the lessons learned from that loss last year into next Saturday's game.

"We learned how it is to play on a Saturday afternoon, we learned the stakes," he said. "We remember how close we were last year and how bad it was to lose that way."

Stuarts Draft's season came to a close in the Region 2B championship. Strasburg defended its regional championship from a year ago with a 35-14 win over Stuarts Draft Nov. 27.

Quincy Williams rushed for 322 yards and five touchdowns in the win. Williams became Strasburg's all-time leader in rushing yards and touchdowns with his performance.

Stuarts Draft finished the season 8-4, falling in the regional title game for the second straight year.

The Cougars had 184 yards passing from quarterback Jake Yow, just a sophomore. Yow was 16-for-31 with three interceptions.

The ground game was slowed most of the night with Draft finishing with 73 yards on the ground.

Senior Baylor Graber led Draft with 41 yards rushing and a touchdown.

#2628. Brewers bash champion Dodgers to brink of NLCS sweep; CBS Sports Preseason All-America team revealed

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2627. Sixers Bell Ringer: LeBron records fifth straight 20-point game in blowout vs. Pacers

Sixers Bell Ringer Season Standings:VJ Edgecombe – 4Jaylen Brown – 3.5Tyrese Maxey – 3.5Joel Embiid – 3LeBron James – 3Anfernee Simons – 1Dean Wade – 1

The Philadelphia 76ers will be in the knockout stage of the NBA Cup.

By beating the Indiana Pacers 111-87, the Sixers clinch Group B in the East, finishing pool play 3-1.

It was a rough night from Tyrese Maxey, shooting 3-13 for only 14 points, but LeBron James, Joel Embiid and company picked up the star's off night.

The Sixers jumped out to a couple early leads, and withstood counter-runs from the Pacers by exploding in the third quarter. They ballooned the lead from 11 at halftime to 27 by the end of the frame.

It will be a red-eye flight to Houston for the Sixers as they are slated to play the Rockets tomorrow.

LeBron James: 21 points, 8-of-13 FG, 3-of-6 3PT, 7 rebounds, 6 assists, 1 block

James set the tone early, carrying over his scorching hot three-point shot from the past two games. He hit his first three attempts from deep, and helped the Sixers establish their first lead of the game singlehandedly.

He continued to display his all-universe passing ability, finding cutting Sixers all over the floor, especially Edgecombe and Embiid in the pocket.

He got comfortable in the midrange in the first half, and was attacking the rim through tough defense, drawing a couple fouls in the process.

It was his fifth straight game scoring 20 or more, securing it with a strong finish through Jarace Walker in the fourth.

Joel Embiid: 14 points, 5-of-14 FG, 1-of-3 3PT, 11 rebounds, 3 assists, 3 steals

It was not Embiid's most prolific outing yet it was great to see him get to his spots. He hit open shots off the catch and was persistently attacking even with a defender like Zubac in front of him. He had a beautiful post spin at the free throw line in the second quarter.

His consistent play was crucial with Maxey being aggressively defended by the Pacers. He picked up three steals, and despite letting a couple defensive rebounds turn into offensive rebounds, maintained a defensive prescence inside.

Anfernee Simons: 19 points, 7-of-14 FG, 5-of-12 3PT, 3 assists, 2 rebounds, 1 steal

Simons hot shooting continued against the Pacers. He hit a three in the first half and then four in the third quarter to help put the game way out of reach by the final frame. He kept it up to begin the fourth with a nice running layup over Siakam.

Simons has been a weapon off the bench, and he survived defensively tonight against the struggling Pacers.

Mike Brown exposes a New York Knicks issue they need to address this season originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

After their loss to the Miami Heat, the New York Knicks have had their six-game winning streak snapped, and their defense of the NBA Cup has ended because they are out of the competition.

It was a double-whammy for the Knicks because they wanted to defend their Cup win from 2025, but now they will have to focus on the big one, the NBA championship. That can become even harder because head coach Mike Brown has seen a potentially significant problem for the team.

While slower basketball is great for the Playoffs, the Knicks do still have to perform better when it comes to the regular season. They are still relatively strong with a 12-7 record, but teams might exploit their weakness.

MORE: Mike Brown loved how the Knicks have bounced back from the 0-3 start

As a champion head coach, Brown wants to maximize everything for his team. The Knicks have the talent to keep up with anyone, and they could pick up the pace with their group. This means that Brown wants his team to play faster without sacrificing their effectiveness and efficiency.

"We have to do a better job of figuring out how we can be more consistent. We go through lulls where our pace isn't good. We're about last in pace right now. We go through lulls where we don't score. That makes it tough defensively," Brown said after the Knicks' loss to Miami.

Jalen Brunson and the rest of the Knicks will have to resolve this problem. If they want to keep succeeding, they will need to have a strong campaign, so they can continue their mission to repeat as champions.

#2624. Mike McCarthy admits he hasn't spent enough time with the defense

After registering an unlikely 27-5 win over the previously 8-2 Broncos, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn't angry, resentful, or defiant.

He was the same guy he always is, and he admitted that (as former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said this week), McCarthy hasn't been sufficiently invested in the side of the ball that isn't his personal expertise.

"I have not spent enough time with the defense," McCarthy told reporters. "You know, and that's something that, as far as job responsibility, job description, you know, these are things that'll be looked at in the offseason. But, you know, it's a point in our year where we're making adjustments and definitely conscientious of it. But at the end of the day, we have to all do our jobs and make sure we're giving the players the plan and all the other things that they need that we can perform and play with that type of urgency, physicality that we played today."

McCarthy prefaced his comments with a lesson he learned as a boy, growing up in Pittsburgh.

"My father used to tell me all the time as a kid, 'You tell the truth, you only have to tell your story once,'" McCarthy said.

The truth is that this week has entailed two sharply different versions of reality, where both things can indeed be the truth. One, McCarthy (like all of us) has flaws. Two, Rodgers should not have spoken about them publicly.

Rodgers clumsily defended his decision to break the code of a football locker room by texting this to Al Michaels: "The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership."

That's fine, but how does disregarding the "sanctity" of the locker room (a word Rodgers undoubtedly selected in response to Tom Brady using it on Thursday) create "accountability"? McCarthy is accountable to team owner Art Rooney II. Not to the media or the fans.

And to what end? He was either doing it to help the Steelers save their season, or he was lashing out.

We'll let you decide which explanation is more likely.

Grant Nelson walks down court during the Emirates NBA Cup Group Play against the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum on Nov. 25, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Getty Images

Nelson, 24, got the call-up at the start of the Nets' four-game road trip, making his season debut in a brief cameo at Minnesota. In the first meaningful non-tanking minutes of his career, Nelson actually helped the Nets to a 104-97 victory. He had just one point but added six rebounds, including three on the offensive glass, and was a plus-six in 13:04.

"You saw Grant: You plug him in, and he does everything well. His size, how smart he is, skilled, tough — really, really tough," head coach Jordi Fernández said. So he's playing really hard, playing with a lot of good energy, and it's contagious."

Grant Nelson (16) and Egor Demin (8) play defense during the game against the Toronto Raptors during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on Nov. 27, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

For a Brooklyn team that has shown a disappointing lack of hustle and energy, Nelson provided plenty.

Nelson was an undrafted 2025 rookie, and other than four NBA cameos he spent the season in the G-League working at forward and center. But this year he was exclusively a center, averaging 16.8 points and 11.8 boards on 57.4 percent shooting before getting called up.

"Continuing to work on my game, still making that transition to a five man, so being able to guard in the perimeter, still working on that jump shot. Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs defeated Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 tonight in a clash of MVP frontrunners during a must-win game to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals.

The Lakers had a 20-point lead in what looked like a blowout game in the first half before the Spurs turned things around in the third quarter to steal the win.

After the game, Luka Doncic was walking off the floor when a couple seemingly shouted something at him, which he took exception to and threw his wristband at them in frustration, hitting the wife.

Subsequently, the Slovenian superstar went back to retrieve his elbow pad when her husband shoved Doncic. Jarred Vanderbilt and the arena security staff intervened to defuse the situation.

WILD SCENE on the way to the locker room. Fans say Luka Dončić tossed a wristband toward a fan on his way to the locker room, went back to get it, and an angry Spurs fan responded by shoving him. 👀

— SpursRΞPORTΞR (@SpursReporter) November 28, 2026

During the postgame press conference, Luka Doncic addressed this incident with the Spurs fan.

"I just threw my wristband as I do after every game. And I heard them say, 'Tsk, I don't want it,' so I went back to grab it, and then he just pushed me, so I gave it to somebody else," Doncic said.

This incident went viral on social media as some fans were shocked to see an opposing supporter could end up shoving a player like this. But mostly others also believed that the husband's response was justified, as Doncic's gesture could be perceived as disrespectful in that moment.

"Luka deserved that push. Threw it at them, then snatched it after they tried to just give it back politely. Such a sore loser & a crybaby."

Doncic ended the night with 31 points, eight assists, and six rebounds while shooting 14-31 from the field (45.2% FG). But that was not enough to stop the Lakers from falling to 15-4 tonight.

The Lakers will now face the Grizzlies on Sunday, November 29. The Spurs will host the Celtics on the same night.

#2619. Spurs erase 20-point deficit to eliminate Lakers in NBA Cup action, advance to knockout round as wild card

The most wide-open division of the 2026 NBA Cup entering Friday, the final day of group play, was West Group C, which had four different teams capable of clinching a spot in the knockout rounds. Two of those teams were the San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers, and they delivered one of the night's wildest games.

The Spurs erased a 20-point deficit on their way to a 99-96 win over the Lakers, riding another huge game from Victor Wembanyama. The win officially put them in the knockout rounds as the West's wild card, thanks to a plus-57 point differential in four games.

Simultaneously, the Portland Trail Blazers won the group by defeating the Golden State Warriors and holding the tiebreaker over San Antonio. The Lakers and Warriors were eliminated with the losses.

Wembanyama finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, 4 steals, 2 assists and 2 blocks, but his 3-for-8 night at the line also invited disaster toward the end of the game, when the Lakers were trying to inch their way back into it.

Los Angeles got the ball down three with a chance to tie the game twice in the final 10 seconds, but the Spurs fouled both times and managed to hold on for the win.

It was a brutal first half for the Spurs, who entered halftime down 54-38, but they proceeded to outscore the Lakers 30-14 in the third quarter and continued that momentum into the fourth quarter to take control.

It's a return to knockout-round action for the Spurs, who reached the NBA Cup championship game last year before losing to the New York Knicks (a result that was repeated in the NBA Finals). They will now face the Dallas Mavericks, the only team to go undefeated in group play, in the quarterfinals next week.

#2618. Jets getting much-needed defensive reinforcement with David Onyemata’s return

Three years ago, David Onyemata missed three games with an ankle injury. In 2020, the defensive tackle missed one game with a calf injury.

Those four games represented the entirety of his injury-related absences during his first 10 years in the NFL.

However, it has been nearly 10 weeks since the 33-year-old has taken the field — following core-muscle surgery — after just two appearances with the Jets.

"It's part of the business," Onyemata said. "Things like this happen. You try not to think too much about it. You just try to stay involved mentally and physically; just be present in the moment and present for the guys."

Though Onyemata is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Miami, the veteran — who was a full participant in practice all week — told The Post that he will return to the field for the first time since Week 2.

Jets defensive lineman David Onyemata practices during training camp on Aug. 17, 2026, in Florham Park, N.J. Bill Kostroun/New York Post

"I feel great," Onyemata said. "Getting back out there, getting in the rhythm of things and being with the guys has been great."

Onyemata — who came from Atlanta on a one-year, $10.5 million deal — was a much-needed 300-pound addition, signed to help overhaul a defense that finished 29th in the league against the run in head coach Aaron Glenn's first season.

Last season, Onyemata — who played for the Saints when Glenn was a defensive coach there — ranked eighth overall and against the run, out of 127 interior defensive linemen, according to Pro Football Focus.

The Nigeria-born defender has played just 45 snaps with the Jets, who rank 30th in the league in rushing yards allowed per game (137.4) and tied for last in rushing first downs allowed per game (8.3).

"[He's] a veteran presence and someone that knows the system inside and out," Glenn said Friday. "Extremely tough, extremely violent, and there is a trust there."

Glenn's defensive line could also soon be boosted by the return of T'Vondre Sweat (knee), who was placed on injured reserve following the Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.

Jets defensive lineman David Onyemata speaks to reporters after a training practice on Aug. 17, 2026 in Florham Park, N.J. Bill Kostroun/New York Post

The 25-year-old, 366-pound defensive tackle — who was acquired from the Titans in an offseason trade for Jermaine Johnson — opened his 21-day practice window this week and was a full participant in every session since Wednesday, but he is listed as questionable.

Glenn made it clear how much it would mean for the defense to bring back the former second-round pick, who has 17 tackles and seven quarterback pressures in seven games (six starts) this season.

"When it comes to Sweat, when you build your defense, you want to build it through the middle, and he's a guy that we always felt could be that key cog in the middle of our defense," Glenn said. "Both of those guys we've talked about at length about what they bring to the table."

Their absences have been especially glaring in the past three games, as the Jets have allowed an average of 174 yards rushing on 5.6 yards per carry.

In last month's loss to the Dolphins, Ollie Gordon II ran for a season-high 103 yards and a touchdown. This weekend, Miami may lean on the running back even more, with Kyle McCord set to make his third career start at quarterback.

"I think they're doing a good job of keeping it simple and saying, 'Hey we're gonna do it this way and we're gonna beat you doing some simple things,' " Jets defensive tackle Harrison Phillips said. "They've found their rhythm running the football a little bit more … I think it's a little bit more of a hard-nosed, 'Hey, we might even be telling you what we're gonna do. Can you stop it?' "

#2615. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

#2614. Lakers go cold in second half and lose to the Spurs

Victor Wembanyama slammed a reverse two-handed dunk over Walker Kessler. On the next play, he volleyball spiked Collin Sexton's layup attempt into the front row at Frost Bank Center. San Antonio fans wagged their index fingers toward the court.

The "MVP" chants that so often greet Luka Doncic even in visiting arenas belong to the Spurs' French superstar here.

Wembanyama's 25 points and 16 rebounds led the Spurs to a 99-96 comeback win over the Lakers on Friday in a thrilling matchup between the top two teams in the Western Conference. The Lakers (15-4) squandered a 20-point first-half lead that cost them a spot in the NBA Cup knockout round. Instead of advancing to the quarterfinals of the in-season tournament, the Lakers will play two regular-season matchups in two weeks.

The quarterfinals on Dec. 4-5 are set: Boston-Detroit, Philadelphia-Atlanta, San Antonio-Dalla, Memphis-Portland.

Doncic had 31 points, eight assists and six rebounds, but he continues to struggle on three-point shots. He entered Friday's game shooting 26.6% from three during the last five games and went just one for 13 from beyond the arc in the much-anticipated showdown.

The Lakers, who led by 20 with 4:43 left in the second quarter and 16 at halftime, got an uneven return from Austin Reaves. The guard who missed the last five games because of a left heel bruise had 21 points and eight rebounds with seven turnovers, but was held to just two points in the first half. He scored 13 in the fourth quarter, including a three with 34 seconds to go that brought the Lakers to within three before the Spurs inched away from the free-throw line.

Lakers guard Luka Doncic, putting up a shot against Spurs guard Dylan Harper, finished with 31 points on Friday night but only made one of 13 three-point shots. (Ronald Cortes / Getty Images)

The Lakers went 4-1 without Reaves and remained atop the NBA standings entering Friday. But the Lakers lead the league with outside skepticism. They had only played eight games against teams currently better than .500. They hadn't played a winning team since narrowly surviving a comeback attempt from the Atlanta Hawks on the road on Nov. 9. Three games — at San Antonio, Memphis and Houston — on their current four-game trip could serve as early statement opportunities.

The Lakers looked every bit the championship contenders they hoped to be during the first half. They ended the first quarter on an 8-0 run that chewed up more than four minutes. Despite Doncic struggling with his three-point shot early, missing his first six shots from distance, he still orchestrated the Lakers to a 13-point first-quarter lead.

The Lakers fought to keep the Spurs (16-4) scoreless even when playing without Kessler against Wembanyama. The French superstar got swarmed by Jarred Vanderbilt, Sandro Mamukelashvili and even switched onto 6-foot-5 guard Quentin Grimes yet was held to just two points and three rebounds during the first quarter.

With the Lakers clogging the paint, Wembanyama was forced to move outside. He made the Spurs' first three-pointer of the game, ending the team's 0-for-10 start from beyond the arc with 2:57 remaining in the second quarter. The Spurs were the third-best three-point shooting team in the league entering Friday's game at 33.4%, but were held to a season-low 38 first-half points.

They nearly equaled that total in a dominant third quarter in which they outscored the Lakers 30-14. The Spurs made three-of-eight threes during the quarter and tied the score on a corner three from Keldon Johnson with two seconds left.

The reigning Western Conference champions led the league with 48.4 rebounds per game but got outrebounded during the first half 24-15. The Spurs won the rebounding battle 47-43 and got the dagger three-pointer from Stephon Castle with 43 seconds remaining off an offensive rebound after a missed free throw by Wembanyama. Instead of a chance to tie the score, the Lakers got the ball back down by six.

#2612. Rams sign tight end away NFC West rival’s practice squad

The Los Angeles Rams are turning to a familiar NFC West rival for help at tight end. Following unfortunate injury news involving Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles has signed veteran tight end Jack Stoll off the San Francisco 49ers' practice squad, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

The move comes at an important time for Sean McVay's offense, which has suddenly lost two of its key tight end options. Allen suffered a high ankle sprain that is expected to sideline him for multiple weeks, while Higbee is dealing with a chest contusion and is considered week-to-week.

With Terrance Ferguson already on injured reserve, the Rams needed additional depth behind Colby Parkinson and rookie Max Klare. Stoll provides an experienced option who can contribute as both a blocker and pass catcher.

Stoll originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Nebraska in 2021, signing with the Philadelphia Eagles. He spent his first three seasons in Philadelphia, helping the organization reach Super Bowl LVII.

His career took several turns in 2024. After signing with the New York Giants that offseason, Stoll was released during final roster cuts. He returned to Philadelphia's practice squad before being eventually claimed off waivers by the Miami Dolphins.

In 2025, Stoll signed with the New Orleans Saints, where he appeared in 15 games, including four starts. He later signed with the Cleveland Browns in March 2026 but did not make their final roster. Afterward, he landed on the 49ers' practice squad in September before the Rams came calling on Thanksgiving.

Across 77 regular-season appearances, Stoll has recorded 28 receptions for 239 yards and one touchdown. His best statistical season came in 2022 with Philadelphia, when he caught 11 passes for 123 yards.

Stoll isn't expected to replace the receiving production of Allen or Higbee. However, his experience as a blocking tight end could prove valuable as the Rams navigate another difficult stretch of injuries.

It's only a matter of time. Stoll will probably be active for Week 13 but playing time will be determined based on how quickly he can acclimate with the playbook. Stoll's strength as a run blocker signals that Sean McVay is committed to 13 personnel and with the Rams only having Colby Parkinson and Max Klare, it is imperative that they have depth behind those two. Dan Villari could be an option as the third tight end if Stoll is not ready to go.

#2611. 10 Takeaways: Avalanche’s Comeback in Minnesota Was One for the Record Books

The Colorado Avalanche pulled off one of the most improbable wins in franchise history on Friday night.

Down three goals with just 6:23 remaining in the third period, the Avalanche rallied to beat the Minnesota Wild 4-3 in a shootout at Grand Casino Arena. They did it without Nathan MacKinnon or Martin Necas, against one of the top teams in the league.

Read NextPostgame Reaction: Avalanche Rally From Three-Goal Deficit to Beat Wild in Shootout

1. This was the latest three-goal comeback victory in Avalanche history. They've never completed a comeback this large with less time on the clock.

2. It was also just the fourth three-goal, third-period comeback victory in franchise history. The last time Colorado accomplished the feat was Dec. 3, 2024, which many will remember as Scott Wedgewood's debut with the Avalanche. He entered the game in relief in Buffalo and helped lead Colorado to a victory after being down 4-1.

This record applies strictly to the regular season. Wild fans, of course, remember Game 5 of the second round of the playoffs last spring just as well as Avalanche fans do.

3. This game was another reminder of why taking advantage of empty-net opportunities is so important. The Wild had a chance to put the game away when they were leading 3-1. Matt Boldy and Kirill Kaprizov were involved in a play with an opportunity to score into the empty net, but they couldn't get the puck through. Cale Makar was part of the defensive effort that stopped the play.

Not long afterward, Makar put the puck on net, and Artturi Lehkonen redirected it past Jesper Wallstedt to make it 3-2.

4. Makar was all over this game, and it went well beyond his crucial assist and eventual shootout-deciding goal. He played more than 27 minutes and looked like the best version of himself, both defensively and with the puck. With MacKinnon sidelined, this is Makar's team for the next few months, and he has looked great in the two games since returning from his injury.

5. T.J. Hughes continues to look more comfortable in the NHL with each passing game. He had his fingerprints all over Friday's comeback, and his recent production is starting to reflect how much his game has developed. Hughes now has one goal, 10 assists, and 11 points over his last 11 games. He had just four points in his first 14 games.

Read NextMartin Necas Out For Avalanche Against Minnesota Wild

6. I've never seen a player put in this much work in such a short period of time. Behind the scenes, Hughes is one of the most difficult players to catch for an interview after practices or morning skates. Not because he's uninterested in talking. Quite the opposite. He's one of the friendliest and most willing players to speak with media.

Hughes stays on the ice longer than anyone I've ever seen. And it's not occasional. It's almost every single time. Most, if not all, of his teammates have already left the locker room before Hughes finally gets off the ice.

7. Remember the debate throughout the summer about whether Jared Bednar would actually play the kids? Well, Hughes has given him a pretty good reason to keep playing him.

8. Devon Toews continues to do Norris Trophy-caliber things. He's now up to 10 goals on the season. Somehow, he's playing even better hockey than he was two weeks ago, when he was already on an incredible run.

Toews is averaging 25:06 of ice time over his last five games. Some of that workload came with Makar out of the lineup. But Makar is back, and Toews is still logging massive minutes.

9. Just like that, the Avalanche are sixth in the NHL in points percentage. They're working their way back up the standings and, more importantly, playing much more consistent and responsible hockey.

10. I'm really curious to know what the sequence of events was with Martin Necas ahead of Friday's game. Taylor Makar getting recalled before the team traveled Thursday made me wonder. I had a feeling someone else might be coming out of the lineup.

But Necas still traveled with the team to Minnesota. He was there, but ultimately didn't play. If the Avalanche knew for certain he wasn't going to be available, it seems unlikely he would have made the trip.

That makes me think this is more of a day-to-day thing. We'll find out more on Saturday.

10 Takeaways: Devon Toews Continues to Quietly Put Together a Special Season (+)

10 Takeaways: Scott Wedgewood Gives Avalanche the Performance They Needed (+)

10 Takeaways: Too Many Guys Had Off Nights For Avalanche

#2609. Things get physical as Spurs fan shoves Luka Doncic in wild exchange with Lakers star

The Los Angeles Lakers couldn't hold on to a 20-point lead Friday night, and Luka Doncic couldn't hold on to his temper.

Moments after the San Antonio Spurs stunned the Lakers with a 99-96 comeback victory in their NBA Cup Group C matchup, Doncic got into a heated altercation with two courtside fans that required security to intervene.

Video captured by Amazon Prime Video's postgame broadcast showed Doncic walking toward the visitors' locker room when a woman sitting courtside appeared to say something to the Lakers superstar.

Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts during a game against the San Antonio Spurs in San Antonio, Texas, Friday, Nov. 27th, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Doncic dismissively tossed his white wristband at the woman before continuing toward the tunnel. Seconds later, he doubled back to retrieve it.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic #77 is shoved by a Spurs' fan sitting courtside in San Antonio. Amazon Prime

The woman's male companion, who had picked up the wristband, handed it back to Doncic before shoving the five-time All-Star with his right hand as he walked away.

Doncic stopped in his tracks and turned around, but Lakers teammate Jarred Vanderbilt restrained him before leaning toward the fan and exchanging words.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic #77 is shoved by a Spurs' fan sitting courtside in San Antonio.

Security quickly intervened, and the male fan was subsequently ejected while Doncic retreated to the Lakers' locker room.

It's unclear what was initially said to Doncic, but throwing his wristband at a spectator was an unnecessary lapse in judgment. That, however, doesn't give a paying customer license to put his hands on an NBA player.

With the entire incident captured on camera, Doncic could face a fine or suspension from the NBA. It's unknown whether the fan will face additional punishment.

The altercation punctuated a spectacular collapse by the Lakers, whose 20-point first-half advantage evaporated like water on hot pavement. San Antonio outscored Los Angeles 30-14 in the third quarter, tying the game entering the fourth before pulling off the upset.

The Lakers lost their composure long before Doncic reached the tunnel.

#2607. Malik Nabers a top Giants receiver without knowing ‘what’s a catch nowadays’

One of the NFL's best receivers doesn't know a catch from a non-catch.

Malik Nabers knows he makes a lot of big receptions for the Giants, but he is just as confused as every NFL fan once replay review gets involved. The 100-catch weapon is trying to figure out how in just the last six days … he lost a first-down catch, the Jaguars' Parker Washington lost a touchdown catch against the Giants, the Rams' Konata Mumpfield lost a touchdown catch, and the Chiefs' Rashee Rice lost a game-changing first down.

"When you go to the ground, the ball is going to move. It's going to move," Nabers said. "It doesn't mean that you dropped the ball. I don't know what's a catch nowadays. I guess you just have to not let the ball even touch the ground. You just have to hope it doesn't. Roll your body up so it doesn't. I guess you have to be more conscious now."

Nabers admittedly was nervous when an airborne Washington dragged both feet in the end zone as the Jaguars rallied against the Giants last week. But the ball moved as he crashed to the ground.

"When Parker made that catch, everybody was like 'Not in!'" Nabers said. "I watched that. I was like, 'No, he's in. Oh, my God.' When they called it [incomplete], I literally was like, 'What is a catch if that's not a catch?'"

Head coach John Harbaugh and tight end Isaiah Likely, who both joined Nabers in New York this season, understand Nabers' confusion on a personal level. Harbaugh's Ravens lost to the Steelers last season when a 13-yard catch was ruled incomplete because Likely didn't finish a third step before the ball was jarred loose.

Does Harbaugh know what a catch looks like?

"I thought I did," Harbaugh said. "Now it goes to replay, and I don't know. Once it goes to replay, it gets all real gray. That was the same way last year, so that hasn't changed."

Malik Nabers catches a pass in front of Antonio Johnson (6) of the Jacksonville Jaguars for a second-quarter touchdown. Getty Images

That's not going to stop the Giants from throwing the ball to Nabers, especially when he is lined up in the slot.

Nabers (65 catches for 747 yards and three drops) is averaging 14.8 air yards per target out of the slot, ranked No. 5 in the NFL among wide receivers with at least 15 slot targets, per NextGenStats. He has caught nine of 14 downfield targets (10-plus air yards) for 247 yards (No. 3) and three touchdowns (tied for No. 2).

"It's just tough to match him up in there," Harbaugh said. "He's good against zone. He's good against man. I think we've schemed some really good things up for him, and Isaiah also has been really good in the slot. It's tough to find a way to cover those guys in the slot, so we try to get them in there and get them open."

Nabers has accumulated 47 percent (353) of his receiving yards from the slot despite nearly one-third as many targets on the inside (26) as out wide (70). It seems to be the go-to way to feature Nabers in the red zone.

Parker Washington attempts to catch a pass in front of Dru Phillips during the fourth quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 22, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Getty Images

"It's a natural way to try to remove some of the cloud [coverage], some of the double-teams," Nabers said. "I still can get doubled in the slot — I still do. Putting me in the slot, motioning me … creates a better matchup — a wider split, a two-way release, giving me an opportunity to do stuff on their nickel or on their safeties or on their linebackers."

Case in point: The Giants drew up a mismatch of Nabers in the slot against Jaguars safety Antonio Johnson last week. Easy touchdown.

"The coaches spend a lot of time studying defense trying to get us open," Nabers said. "I didn't really think they were going to play that defense. Me being in the slot, I thought somebody was going to follow me or about to double me. When I got that coverage, I was like, 'Oh, it's just like practice.' And I took advantage of it."

The Giants had Wan'Dale Robinson in the slot during Nabers' first two seasons. Now, with rookie Malachi Fields and Darnell Mooney, there is more opportunity for Nabers to get creative.

"It's a credit to him," quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan said. "Not every receiver can handle that. It puts a lot of mental stress on with formations, motions, shifts, where you have to be, what route you are running. To see him able to handle that and still go out the way he played has been awesome."

#2604. Luka Dončić shoved by fan in bizarre wristband-tossing incident after Lakers' loss to Spurs

The Los Angeles Lakers blowing a 20-point lead against the San Antonio Spurs on Friday was bad. What happened immediately after was ugly, with Lakers star Luka Dončić getting shoved by a courtside fan.

The incident began when Dončić tossed an armband at a female fan who appeared to be jeering him as he walked by. Dončić took a few more steps, then turned around and got the wristband back from a male fan, who picked up the armband then gave Dončić a one-armed shove as the All-Star started walking away.

Dončić immediately turned around, but Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt stepped in front of him while a few staffers immediately surrounded the male fan.

It's unknown what was said before and after the shove, but the NBA will certainly be looking into it.

For his part, Dončić told reporters after the game that he went back to the fans because they told him they didn't want his wristband:

"I threw my wristband, like I do almost every game, and then I heard they didn't want it, so I went to try to grab it and he just pushed me. Then I gave it to somebody else."

Before the incident, Dončić posted 31 points on 14-of-31 shooting with 8 assists, 6 rebounds, 3 steals and 3 turnovers in a 99-96 loss for the Lakers, who had won 11 of their last 12 games entering Friday. The loss officially eliminated the Lakers from the NBA Cup, as they finished with a 2-2 record in group play.

#2601. Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

#2599. Lakers blow 20-point lead in NBA Cup loss to Spurs in biggest test of season

SAN ANTONIO — JJ Redick, and the rest of the Lakers, acknowledged the four-game road trip would be a "massive challenge" because of different tests each team would present.

The biggest test of the trip, and the season so far, came Friday night at Frost Bank Center in the form of Spurs, the reigning Western Conference champions.

And for the first 19 minutes, the Lakers looked like a team ready to ace the test. But the problems they had to answer evolved, and they didn't find enough solutions, leading to the Lakers blowing a 20-point lead and suffering a 99-96 loss to the Spurs to close out NBA Cup group play.

Victor Wembanyama, who scored 25 points and grabbed 16 rebounds, celebrates during the Lakers' 99-96 NBA Cup loss to the Spurs on Nov. 27, 2026, in San Antonio. AP

The Lakers fell to 15-4 with the defeat, with the Spurs improving to 16-4 in a battle between the top two teams in the Western Conference.

And though neither Luka Dončić nor Victor Wembanyama had an efficient offensive performance, the Spurs star big man got the bragging rights, at least for one night, in the battle between two of the top contenders for MVP.

Dončić had 31 points, eight assists and six rebounds, but made just 1 of his 13 3-point attempts (14 for 31 from the field) on a night the Lakers struggled with their outside shooting — especially in the second half.

The Lakers shot 28.6% on 3s (6 of 21) in the final two quarters, with the returning Austin Reaves being the only Laker who found a consistent rhythm from beyond the arc.

Reaves (21 points, eight rebounds on 8-of-15 shooting) made all five of his 3s in the second half, including two late in the fourth to keep the game close after struggling with his ball security (seven of Lakers' 20 turnovers).

Wembanyama led the Spurs with 25 points (10-of-25 shooting) and 16 rebounds, while Stephon Castle had team-highs of 26 points and nine assists.

Luka Dončić, who scored 31 points, dribbles up court during the Lakers' 99-96 road loss to the Spurs. NBAE via Getty Images

The Lakers dominated the Spurs early, with nearly flawless execution of their defensive game plan to play off San Antonio's struggling 3-pointer shooters and shrink the floor against Wembanyama.

They held the Spurs to 38.9% shooting in the opening quarter, including 0 for 6 on 3s after the Spurs missed their final six shots (four 3s) of the first.

The Lakers' defensive intensity carried over into the second, with their stout halfcourt defense helping them take a 45-25 lead midway through the quarter before the Spurs cut their deficit to 54-38 going into halftime.

But the script flipped going into the third for the Lakers, who experienced their own offensive struggles. The Lakers scored 14 points on 6-for-24 shooting (2 for 13 on 3s) in the third, with the Spurs tying the game at 68 apiece when Keldon Johnson made a corner 3 with two seconds left in the third.

The Spurs led by as many as eight points in the fourth, but Reaves and Dončić made big shots late to keep the game close before the Spurs closed them out.
